knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cone of globally nonnegative polynomials is
\[
\mathcal{P}_+(\mathbb{R}^n):=\left\{p\in\mathbb{R}[x]:p(u)\ge 0\text{ for every }u\in\mathbb{R}^n\right\}.
\]
It is a convex cone: whenever \(p,q\in\mathcal{P}_+(\mathbb{R}^n)\) and \(a,b\ge 0\), one has \(ap+bq\in\mathcal{P}_+(\mathbb{R}^n)\). Global nonnegativity is pointwise and does not itself require a sum-of-squares representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial is globally nonnegative when its value is nonnegative at every real point; such polynomials form a convex cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Globally Nonnegative Polynomials

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SOS polynomials and bounded-degree monomial vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines SOS polynomials and the standard vector of all monomials of bounded total degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial \(p\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\) is a sum-of-squares polynomial, written \(p\in\Sigma[\mathbf x]\), if there exist a finite index set \(J\) and polynomials \(p_j\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\) such that \(p(\mathbf x)=\sum_{j\in J}p_j(\mathbf x)^2\) for every \(\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n\). Every SOS polynomial is globally nonnegative. If \(p\neq0\), then \(\deg p\) is even and every nonzero summand satisfies \(\deg p_j\leq \deg(p)/2\). For \(d\in\mathbb N_0\), define \(\mathbb N_{0,d}^n=\{\boldsymbol\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\boldsymbol\alpha|\le d\}\). Then \(\mathbf v_d(\mathbf x)=(\mathbf x^{\boldsymbol\alpha})_{\boldsymbol\alpha\in\mathbb N_{0,d}^n}\) is the monomial-basis vector for \(\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_d\) and has \(s(d)=\binom{n+d}{d}\) entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real polynomial is SOS if it is a finite sum of squares of real polynomials. Every SOS polynomial is globally nonnegative. A nonzero SOS polynomial has even degree, and each nonzero polynomial being squared has degree at most half that degree. The vector v_d contains all monomials of total degree at most d and has binomial(n+d,d) entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\in\Sigma[\mathbf x]\iff \exists\text{ finite }J,\ (p_j)_{j\in J}:\ p=\sum_{j\in J}p_j^2;\qquad \dim\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_d=\binom{n+d}{d}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polynomial \(p\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) is a sum of squares if there exist an integer \(r\ge 0\) and polynomials \(q_1,\ldots,q_r\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) such that
\[
p=\sum_{j=1}^{r}q_j^2.
\]
The set of all such polynomials is denoted by \(\Sigma[x]\). Every member of \(\Sigma[x]\) is globally nonnegative, so \(\Sigma[x]\subseteq\mathcal{P}_+(\mathbb{R}^n)\); the reverse inclusion need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum-of-squares polynomial is a finite sum of squared real polynomials. Every such polynomial is globally nonnegative, but not conversely.
knowledge_statements.title: Sum-of-Squares Polynomials

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree-bounded SOS certificate for a positive matrix polynomial
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quantitative matrix-polynomial positivity certificate under the stated compact-set assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be the basic semialgebraic set defined by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\), and suppose Assumption 2.14 holds. Let \(\mathbf F\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]^{p\times p}\) be symmetric of degree \(d\). If \(\delta>0\) and \(\mathbf F(\mathbf x)\succeq\delta\mathbf I\) for every \(\mathbf x\in K\), then there are SOS matrix polynomials \(\mathbf F_0,\ldots,\mathbf F_m\) such that \(\mathbf F=\mathbf F_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf F_jg_j\), with \(\deg\mathbf F_0,\deg(\mathbf F_1g_1),\ldots,\deg(\mathbf F_mg_m)\le c\bigl(d^2n^d\|\mathbf F\|/\delta\bigr)^c\), where \(c\) depends only on \((g_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 2.14, every symmetric matrix polynomial that is uniformly positive definite on the basic semialgebraic set has an SOS matrix-polynomial certificate. All certificate terms obey the stated degree bound, with a constant depending only on the defining constraints.
assumptions_latex: K\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is the basic semialgebraic set defined by }g_1,\ldots,g_m
\mathbf F\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]^{p\times p},\quad \mathbf F^T=\mathbf F,\quad \deg\mathbf F=d
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\ \text{SOS matrix polynomials }\mathbf F_0,\ldots,\mathbf F_m:\quad \mathbf F=\mathbf F_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf F_jg_j,\quad \max\{\deg\mathbf F_0,\deg(\mathbf F_jg_j):1\le j\le m\}\le c\left(d^2n^d\frac{\|\mathbf F\|}{\delta}\right)^c

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The basic closed semialgebraic set generated by \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) is
\[
K(g):=\left\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(u)\ge 0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\right\}.
\]
The associated positivity cone is
\[
\mathcal{P}_+(K(g)):=\left\{p\in\mathbb{R}[x]:p(u)\ge 0\text{ for every }u\in K(g)\right\}.
\]
Strict positivity on \(K(g)\) means \(p(u)>0\) for every \(u\in K(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial inequalities define a basic closed semialgebraic set; its positivity cone consists of polynomials nonnegative at every feasible point.
knowledge_statements.title: Positivity on Basic Semialgebraic Sets

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K(g)=K(\widetilde g)\Rightarrow\mathcal P_+(K(g))=\mathcal P_+(K(\widetilde g)),\qquad K(g)=\varnothing\Rightarrow\mathcal P_+(K(g))=\mathbb R[x].
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates the intrinsic positivity cone from a chosen inequality presentation and records the vacuous empty-set case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K(g)=K(\widetilde g)\), then \(\mathcal P_+(K(g))=\mathcal P_+(K(\widetilde g))\). If \(K(g)=\varnothing\), then universal quantification is vacuous and \(\mathcal P_+(K(g))=\mathbb R[x]\). If \(K(g)\ne\varnothing\), then \(-1\notin\mathcal P_+(K(g))\), so the cone is proper.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positivity cone depends only on the underlying set; for an empty set it is the whole polynomial ring, while for a nonempty set it is proper.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
V_{\mathbb{R}}(I):=\left\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:h(u)=0\text{ for every }h\in I\right\}.
\]
A residue class \(p+I\in\mathbb{R}[x]/I\) is nonnegative on the real variety if \(p(u)\ge 0\) for every \(u\in V_{\mathbb{R}}(I)\). This is well defined because any two representatives of \(p+I\) agree on \(V_{\mathbb{R}}(I)\). The resulting cone is denoted by \((\mathbb{R}[x]/I)_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial class modulo an ideal is nonnegative when any representative is nonnegative on the ideal's real zero set.
knowledge_statements.title: Positivity Modulo Polynomial Ideals

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an ideal has no real zeros, every quotient class is nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic lineality and real-radical dependence of semantic quotient positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_I=(\mathbb R[x]/I)_+\). Then \(C_I\cap(-C_I)=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}/I\). Consequently \(C_I\) is pointed exactly when \(I=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}\), and after quotienting its lineality the evaluation order depends only on \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lineality of quotient positivity is the real radical modulo the original ideal, so the cone is pointed exactly for real-radical ideals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_I\cap(-C_I)=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}/I,\qquad C_I\text{ is pointed}\iff I=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The quadratic module generated by \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) is
\[
M(g):=\left\{\sum_{i=0}^{m}\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.
\]
It contains \(1\), is closed under addition, and satisfies \(sM(g)\subseteq M(g)\) for every \(s\in\Sigma[x]\). Since every generator is nonnegative on \(K(g)\), every member of \(M(g)\) is nonnegative there; hence \(M(g)\subseteq\mathcal{P}_+(K(g))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely generated quadratic module consists of an SOS polynomial plus SOS-weighted constraint polynomials, each nonnegative on the constraint set.
knowledge_statements.title: Finitely Generated Quadratic Modules

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is Archimedean}\iff (\exists R>0)\ R-\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j^2\in M\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic module in the real polynomial ring.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the ball-polynomial characterization of the Archimedean property in a real polynomial ring.

source_refs.locator: 2.6.4 Quadratic modules for compact sets p. 74

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quadratic module \(M\) is Archimedean if for every \(p\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) there exists an integer \(N\ge 1\) such that \(N-p\in M\). For polynomial rings, this is equivalent to the existence of \(R>0\) satisfying
\[
R-\|x\|_2^2=R-\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j^2\in M.
\]
If \(M=M(g)\), this condition implies that \(K(g)\) is contained in the closed ball \(\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|u\|_2^2\le R\}\), and therefore is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic module is Archimedean when it contains a bounding ball polynomial; its associated feasible set is then compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Archimedean Quadratic Modules

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6.4 Quadratic modules for compact sets p. 74

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archimedeanity is equivalently the order-unit property, coordinate boundedness inside the module, or containment of a bounding ball polynomial.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines inequality certificates from a quadratic module with arbitrary polynomial multiples of equality constraints.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.3 Sums of ideals and quadratic modules p. 65

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I(h):=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\) and
\[
K(g,h):=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(u)\ge 0\text{ for all }i,\ h_j(u)=0\text{ for all }j\}.
\]
The ideal-augmented quadratic module is
\[
M(g)+I(h)=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sigma_i g_i+\sum_{j=1}^{s}q_jh_j:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x],\ q_j\in\mathbb{R}[x]\right\}.
\]
Every polynomial in this set is nonnegative on \(K(g,h)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ideal-augmented quadratic module adds arbitrary equality-constraint multiples to SOS-weighted inequality certificates, preserving nonnegativity on the constrained set.
knowledge_statements.title: Ideal-Augmented Quadratic Modules

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.3 Sums of ideals and quadratic modules p. 65

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent quotient-ring representation of equality augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=I(h)\) and let \(\pi:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R[x]/I\) be the quotient map. If \(\overline M\) is the quadratic module generated by \(\pi(g_1),\ldots,\pi(g_m)\), then \[\pi(M(g)+I)=\overline M,\qquad M(g)+I=\pi^{-1}(\overline M).\] Thus \(f\in M(g)+I\) exactly when its residue class belongs to the generated quadratic module in the quotient ring.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an equality ideal is equivalent to forming the inequality-generated quadratic module in the quotient ring and taking its inverse image.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R[x]/I\) is the quotient map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi(M(g)+I)=M_{\mathbb R[x]/I}(\pi(g)),\qquad M(g)+I=\pi^{-1}(M_{\mathbb R[x]/I}(\pi(g))).

notation.meaning: Quotient map modulo the equality ideal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the preordering generated by finitely many weak polynomial inequality constraints.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Quadratic Modules and Preorderings p. 60

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)\in\{0,1\}^m\), set \(g^\alpha:=\prod_{i=1}^{m}g_i^{\alpha_i}\). The preordering generated by \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) is
\[
T(g):=\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g^\alpha:\sigma_\alpha\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.
\]
It is closed under addition and multiplication and contains every square. Each \(g^\alpha\) is nonnegative on \(K(g)\), so \(T(g)\subseteq\mathcal{P}_+(K(g))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely generated preordering is the cone of SOS-weighted square-free products of constraint polynomials; all its members are nonnegative on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Finitely Generated Preorderings

Let \(I(h):=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\), let \(g^\alpha:=\prod_{i=1}^{m}g_i^{\alpha_i}\) for \(\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m\), and define

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g^\alpha\Rightarrow p(u)\ge 0\) for every \(u\in K(g)\).

notation.meaning: Square-free constraint product indexed by alpha.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies an exact algebraic witness for membership in a finitely generated preordering.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Quadratic Modules and Preorderings p. 60

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A preordering membership certificate for \(p\) is a family \((\sigma_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\) with each \(\sigma_\alpha\in\Sigma[x]\) such that
\[
p=\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g^\alpha.
\]
The displayed polynomial identity and the sum-of-squares decompositions of the multipliers are finite algebraic witnesses that \(p\in T(g)\). Evaluating the identity at any \(u\in K(g)\) yields \(p(u)\ge 0\), since every summand is nonnegative there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit SOS-weighted constraint-product identity certifies preordering membership and consequently nonnegativity throughout the basic semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.title: Preordering Membership Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Two standard strict-positivity representation regimes are distinguished. If \(K(g)\) is compact, Schmüdgen's theorem gives
\[
f\in T(g).
\]
If the quadratic module \(M(g)\) is Archimedean, Putinar's theorem gives
\[
f\in M(g)\subseteq T(g).
\]
Thus compactness of the basic closed set yields a preordering representation, whereas the Archimedean quadratic-module hypothesis yields a quadratic-module representation. These conclusions concern strict positivity; mere nonnegativity generally requires additional hypotheses or limiting arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polynomial strictly positive on the basic closed set, compactness yields a preordering representation, while an Archimedean quadratic module yields a quadratic-module representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Preordering Representation Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard ball-constraint definition for a finitely generated quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma[x]\) be the cone of sums of squares in \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), and let \(M(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x]\}\). The quadratic module \(M(g)\) is Archimedean when there exists \(R>0\) such that \(R-\sum_{j=1}^n x_j^2\in M(g)\). Equivalently, for every polynomial \(f\), some integer \(N\geq 1\) satisfies \(N+f\in M(g)\) and \(N-f\in M(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic module is Archimedean when it certifies a bounding ball; equivalently, it order-bounds every polynomial by a sufficiently large constant.
knowledge_statements.title: Archimedeanity

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(g)\text{ is saturated}\iff M(g)=\operatorname{Pos}(K)\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by the defining inequalities.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard saturation property for quadratic modules and preorderings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States saturation for the quadratic module generated by a basic closed semialgebraic description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\geq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), define \(\operatorname{Pos}(K)=\{f\in\mathbb R[x]:f(x)\geq0\text{ for all }x\in K\}\). Since every element of \(M(g)\) is nonnegative on \(K\), one always has \(M(g)\subseteq\operatorname{Pos}(K)\). The module is saturated precisely when the reverse inclusion also holds, so every polynomial nonnegative on \(K\), including polynomials having zeros there, possesses a certificate in \(M(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate module is saturated exactly when it contains every polynomial nonnegative on its associated feasible set, not merely every strictly positive polynomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Saturation

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(g)\text{ is stable}\iff\forall d\in\mathbb N\ \exists r(d)\in\mathbb N:\ M(g)\cap\mathbb R[x]_{\leq d}\subseteq M_{r(d)}(g)\).

notation.meaning: Polynomials of degree at most d.
Elements admitting a module representation with every summand of degree at most twice r.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard degree-bounded formulation of stability for finitely generated quadratic modules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses total degree and truncation by the degrees of complete certificate summands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r\in\mathbb N\), set \(M_r(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_0)\leq2r,\ \deg(\sigma_i g_i)\leq2r\}\). The certificate algebra \(M(g)\) is stable if, for every input-degree bound \(d\), there exists \(r(d)\) such that every \(f\in M(g)\) with \(\deg f\leq d\) already belongs to \(M_{r(d)}(g)\). The bound is uniform over coefficients of \(f\) but is attached to the fixed generators \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stability means that bounded-degree members have certificates of uniformly bounded degree, with the bound depending on input degree and the fixed generators.
knowledge_statements.title: Stability of Certificate Algebras

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-degree formulation is coherent and the property content kind fits the leaf, but stability conventions differ across sources. A locator must support the stated total-degree truncation of complete summands and the dependence of the bound on the fixed generators.

notation.meaning: Degree-at-most-d slice of the polynomial ring.
Quadratic-module certificates truncated at summand degree two r.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-degree slice formulation of uniform certificate-degree control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformity is over all module members in one fixed finite input-degree slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(d\in\mathbb N\). Uniform degree control at degree \(d\) means that some \(r_d\in\mathbb N\), independent of the coefficients and positivity margin of \(f\), satisfies \(M(g)\cap\mathbb R[x]_{\leq d}=M_{r_d}(g)\cap\mathbb R[x]_{\leq d}\). Thus every degree-at-most-\(d\) polynomial possessing any representation \(f=\sigma_0+\sum_i\sigma_i g_i\) possesses one with \(\deg(\sigma_0)\leq2r_d\) and \(\deg(\sigma_i g_i)\leq2r_d\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform degree control bounds certificate degrees simultaneously for all module members whose input degree is at most a fixed value.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Degree Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a fixed degree slice, the equality follows from the stated truncation convention and expresses uniform certificate-degree control. The condition kind is appropriate, but an inspectable source is required for this exact convention and terminology.

Certificate cone truncated at order r for the listed generators.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: natural generator-indexed stability function under total-degree truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records degree growth as a function of both input degree and the chosen certificate generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed generating list \(g\), define \(\beta_g(d)=\inf\{r\in\mathbb N:M(g)\cap\mathbb R[x]_{\leq d}\subseteq M_r(g)\}\), using \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Then \(\beta_g\) is nondecreasing, and \(M(g)\) is stable exactly when \(\beta_g(d)<+\infty\) for every \(d\). Because \(M_r(g)\) constrains the individual products \(\sigma_i g_i\), this growth function belongs to the chosen generator presentation; replacing the list can change the truncations and hence the resulting degree bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The least certificate-degree bound is a nondecreasing function of input degree and is tied to the selected generator presentation.
knowledge_statements.title: Generator-Dependent Degree Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generator-indexed function is internally coherent and its monotonicity and stability characterization follow from the definition, but beta_g is introduced without a source and may be local rather than standard notation. A source must also establish whether this leaf should be recorded as a representation or, more specifically, a complexity bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that Archimedeanity is sufficient but not necessary for the strong moment property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the univariate SOS cone \(M=\Sigma[x]\subset\mathbb R[x]\), every linear functional nonnegative on \(M\) has a finite positive Borel representing measure on \(\mathbb R=K_M\) by the Hamburger moment theorem. Hence \(M\) has the strong moment property. It is not Archimedean because \(R-x^2\notin\Sigma[x]\) for every \(R\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The univariate SOS cone has the strong moment property although it is not Archimedean.
assumptions_latex: \(M=\Sigma[x]\subset\mathbb R[x]\) is the cone of sums of squares in one variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ has the strong moment property but is not Archimedean}.

notation.meaning: Cone of sums of squares of real univariate polynomials.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Moment Property without Archimedeanity

assumptions_latex: \(L:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R\) is linear and \(L(h)\geq0\) for every \(h\in M(g)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\mu\geq0\text{ supported on }K:\ L(f)=\int_K f\,d\mu\quad\forall f\in\mathbb R[x]\).

notation.meaning: Basic closed set defined by the generators.
Linear functional dual to the certificate cone.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Archimedean quadratic-module moment representation theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full polynomial moment representation for the dual cone of an Archimedean quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\geq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), and suppose \(M(g)\) is Archimedean. If a linear functional \(L:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(L(h)\geq0\) for every \(h\in M(g)\), then there exists a finite positive Borel measure \(\mu\), supported on \(K\), such that \(L(f)=\int_K f\,d\mu\) for every \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\). Conversely, integration against any finite positive Borel measure supported on \(K\) defines a functional nonnegative on \(M(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Archimedeanity, positive functionals on the certificate cone are exactly moment functionals of finite positive measures supported on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment Properties of Certificate Cones

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is locally appropriate and states the expected Archimedean moment representation, including the converse, but no authoritative theorem locator is supplied. children.title: Hilbert Sum-of-Squares Classification
children.top_down_role: Classical equality and separation regimes for nonnegative and sum-of-squares forms.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists p,q\in\mathbb R[t]:\ f=p^2+q^2\).

notation.meaning: The univariate real polynomial under consideration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Univariate real-polynomial case of Hilbert's sum-of-squares classification.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 Univariate Nonnegative Polynomials p. 85

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(f\in\mathbb R[t]\), global nonnegativity is equivalent to a polynomial sum-of-squares representation: \[f(t)\geq0\text{ for all }t\in\mathbb R\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(t)=p(t)^2+q(t)^2\text{ for some }p,q\in\mathbb R[t].\] The zero polynomial is included. For nonzero \(f\), the condition forces even degree and positive leading coefficient, and the two-square representation can be chosen with \(\deg p,\deg q\leq\deg(f)/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every globally nonnegative real univariate polynomial is a sum of two polynomial squares, and every such sum is globally nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Univariate Global Positivity

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1 Univariate Nonnegative Polynomials p. 85

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Root-Multiplicity Characterization of Global Univariate Nonnegativity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real-factorization criterion equivalent to whole-line nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f\in\mathbb R[t]\setminus\{0\}\), the following are equivalent: \(f(t)\ge0\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\); the leading coefficient of \(f\) is positive and every real root has even multiplicity; and \[f(t)=a\prod_i(t-r_i)^{2m_i}\prod_j\big((t-u_j)^2+v_j^2\big)^{n_j},\qquad a>0,\ v_j>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero real univariate polynomial is globally nonnegative exactly when its leading coefficient is positive and all its real roots have even multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\ge0\text{ on }\mathbb R\iff \operatorname{lc}(f)>0\text{ and every real root has even multiplicity}.\)

notation.meaning: representatives of nonreal conjugate root pairs

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Multiplicity Characterization of Global Univariate Nonnegativity

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\geq0\text{ on }\mathbb R^n\iff A\succeq0\iff\exists B:\ Q(x)=\|Bx\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous quadratic forms over the real numbers.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Ax\) be a real quadratic form with \(A\in\mathbb S^n\). Then \(Q(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(A\succeq0\). This is further equivalent to the existence of a real matrix \(B\) satisfying \(A=B^{\mathsf T}B\), in which case \[Q(x)=\|Bx\|_2^2=\sum_j(b_j^{\mathsf T}x)^2.\] Hence every nonnegative real quadratic form is a sum of squares of real linear forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real quadratic form is globally nonnegative exactly when its matrix is positive semidefinite, equivalently when the form is a sum of squared linear forms.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Form Positivity

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank and Zero Set of a Nonnegative Quadratic Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural consequences of the positive-semidefinite matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Ax\) with \(A\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(r=\operatorname{rank}A\). Then \[\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Q(x)=0\}=\ker A.\] Moreover, \(Q\) is positive definite exactly when \(A\succ0\), and the minimum number of squared real linear forms in a representation of \(Q\) is \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zeros of a nonnegative quadratic form form the kernel of its PSD matrix, and the matrix rank is the minimum number of linear squares needed to represent it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z(Q)=\ker A,\quad Q\text{ is positive definite}\iff A\succ0,\quad \operatorname{sqrank}(Q)=r.\)

notation.meaning: real zero set of the quadratic form
minimum number of squared linear forms representing the form

knowledge_statements.title: Rank and Zero Set of a Nonnegative Quadratic Form

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists P,Q\in\mathbb R[x,y]_d:\ F=P^2+Q^2\).

notation.meaning: Space of homogeneous binary forms of degree d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative homogeneous binary forms over the real numbers.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\in\mathbb R[x,y]\) be a homogeneous binary form of degree \(2d\). Then \(F(x,y)\geq0\) for all \((x,y)\in\mathbb R^2\) if and only if there exist homogeneous forms \(P,Q\in\mathbb R[x,y]_d\) such that \[F(x,y)=P(x,y)^2+Q(x,y)^2.\] Consequently, every nonnegative real binary form is a sum of squares of real forms. A nonzero globally nonnegative binary form necessarily has even degree, so the displayed case covers all nonzero instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative real binary form of even degree is a sum of two squares of real forms of half that degree.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary-Form Positivity

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists q_1,\ldots,q_s\in\mathbb R[x,y,z]_2:\ F=\sum_{j=1}^s q_j^2\).

notation.meaning: Space of real ternary quadratic forms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hilbert's exceptional sum-of-squares case for real ternary quartic forms.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\in\mathbb R[x,y,z]\) be homogeneous of degree \(4\). If \(F(x,y,z)\geq0\) for every \((x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3\), then there exist finitely many homogeneous quadratic forms \(q_1,\ldots,q_s\in\mathbb R[x,y,z]_2\) such that \[F(x,y,z)=\sum_{j=1}^s q_j(x,y,z)^2.\] The converse follows immediately from the representation. Thus nonnegativity and polynomial sum-of-squares membership coincide for real ternary quartics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real ternary quartic is globally nonnegative exactly when it is a sum of squares of real quadratic forms.
knowledge_statements.title: Ternary-Quartic Positivity

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-length refinement of Hilbert's ternary-quartic exactness theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F\in\mathbb R[x,y,z]_4\) is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^3\), then there exist quadratic forms \(q_1,q_2,q_3\in\mathbb R[x,y,z]_2\), some possibly zero, such that \[F=q_1^2+q_2^2+q_3^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative real ternary quartic is a sum of at most three squares of real quadratic forms.

notation.meaning: space of homogeneous ternary forms of degree d

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Square Refinement for Ternary Quartics

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\geq0\text{ on }\mathbb R^3\quad\text{and}\quad M\notin\Sigma[x,y,z]\).

notation.meaning: Cone of sums of squares of real polynomials.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The homogeneous Motzkin sextic witnesses failure beyond Hilbert's exceptional SOS cases.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The homogeneous Motzkin form \[M(x,y,z)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4+z^6-3x^2y^2z^2\] is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^3\), but it cannot be represented as \(\sum_j q_j(x,y,z)^2\) with real polynomials \(q_j\). It is therefore a concrete nonnegative ternary sextic outside the polynomial sum-of-squares cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The homogeneous Motzkin sextic is nonnegative everywhere but is not a sum of polynomial squares, showing that global nonnegativity need not imply SOS membership.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Non-SOS Forms

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists q\in\mathbb R[x]\setminus\{0\},\ p_1,\ldots,p_s\in\mathbb R[x]:\ q^2f=\sum_{j=1}^s p_j^2\).

notation.meaning: Polynomial numerators in the rational SOS representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Artin's solution of Hilbert's seventeenth problem over the real polynomial ring.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) is nonnegative on all of \(\mathbb R^n\), then there exist a nonzero polynomial \(q\in\mathbb R[x]\) and polynomials \(p_1,\ldots,p_s\in\mathbb R[x]\) such that \[q(x)^2f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^s p_j(x)^2.\] Equivalently, in the rational function field, \(f=\sum_{j=1}^s(p_j/q)^2\). The identity is algebraically checkable after clearing denominators and certifies global nonnegativity wherever \(q\neq0\), while the original hypothesis covers its zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every globally nonnegative real polynomial is a sum of squares of rational functions, equivalently a polynomial SOS after multiplication by one squared denominator.
knowledge_statements.title: Artin Rational-SOS Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Soundness of a Cleared-Denominator Artin Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed converse for a cleared-denominator identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(q^2f=\sum_jp_j^2\) for real polynomials with \(q\ne0\), then \(f\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cleared-denominator SOS identity certifies global nonnegativity, including at zeros of the denominator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\ge0\text{ for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Soundness of a Cleared-Denominator Artin Certificate

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Denominator Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a uniform rational-SOS certificate over a fixed family; existence is not asserted for arbitrary families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be a specified family of globally nonnegative polynomials. A uniform-denominator certificate for \(\mathcal F\) is a nonzero polynomial \(D\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) such that, for every \(f\in\mathcal F\), there exist an integer \(r_f\ge 0\) and polynomials \(p_{f,1},\ldots,p_{f,r_f}\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) satisfying \[D(x)^2f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{r_f}p_{f,j}(x)^2.\] The polynomial \(D\) may depend on \(\mathcal F\), but it is independent of the individual choice of \(f\); the number and degrees of the numerator squares may depend on \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform-denominator certificate uses one fixed nonzero polynomial whose square converts every polynomial in a specified nonnegative family into a polynomial sum of squares.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) is a specified family of globally nonnegative polynomials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a nonzero \(D\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) such that \(D^2f\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\) for every \(f\in\mathcal F\).

notation.meaning: Cone of finite sums of polynomial squares.
A common denominator polynomial independent of the member of the family.

source_refs.locator: §2.4.3, “Uniform denominators,” p. 59

source_witnesses.locator: §2.4.3, “Uniform denominators,” p. 59

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Reznick Denominators for Quantitatively Positive Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed-degree family uniformly separated from zero on the sphere admits a common norm-power denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(n,d\) and \(0<m\le M<\infty\). If every degree-\(2d\) form \(F\in\mathcal F\) satisfies \[m\le F(u)\le M\qquad(\|u\|_2=1),\] then there is an \(r\in\mathbb N_0\), depending only on \(n,d,m,M\), such that \[\bigl(x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2\bigr)^rF\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\qquad(F\in\mathcal F).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-degree forms with uniform positive lower and upper spherical bounds share a common Reznick denominator.
assumptions_latex: Every \(F\in\mathcal F\) is a form of the fixed degree \(2d\).
\(m\le F(u)\le M\) uniformly on the unit sphere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For one common \(r\), \(\rho^rF\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\) for every \(F\in\mathcal F\), where \(\rho=\sum_i x_i^2\).

notation.meaning: Uniform spherical lower and upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Reznick Denominators for Quantitatively Positive Families

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Families Admit a Common Denominator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that the genuinely restrictive uniform-denominator question begins with infinite families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F=\{f_1,\ldots,f_N\}\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\). Suppose that for every \(i\) there is a nonzero polynomial \(D_i\) such that \(D_i^2f_i\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\). Then the single nonzero polynomial \(D=\prod_{i=1}^N D_i\) satisfies \(D^2f_i\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\) for every \(i\). In particular, every finite family of globally nonnegative real polynomials has a uniform denominator by Artin's theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying memberwise denominators produces one common denominator for every finite family; nonuniformity can arise only for genuinely infinite families.
assumptions_latex: For each \(i\), \(D_i\ne0\) and \(D_i^2f_i\) is a polynomial sum of squares.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D=\prod_{i=1}^N D_i\Longrightarrow D^2f_i\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\quad(i=1,\ldots,N).

notation.meaning: The product denominator common to the finite family.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Families Admit a Common Denominator

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Properties of a Uniform Denominator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability of a fixed denominator under finite conic combination and multiplication of the denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(D\ne0\) and \(D^2f\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\) for every \(f\in\mathcal F\). Then \(D^2h\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\) for every finite conic combination \(h=\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i f_i\), where \(f_i\in\mathcal F\) and \(\lambda_i\ge0\). Moreover, for every nonzero \(H\in\mathbb R[x]\), \((HD)^2f\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\) for every \(f\in\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common denominator remains valid for the finite conic hull of the family, and every nonzero polynomial multiple of it is another common denominator.
assumptions_latex: Conic combinations are finite with nonnegative real coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D^2\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal F)\subseteq\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2,\qquad (HD)^2f\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\quad(f\in\mathcal F,\ H\ne0).

notation.meaning: Finite nonnegative conic hull of the family.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Properties of a Uniform Denominator

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Soundness at Zeros of a Common Denominator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why a polynomial denominator identity certifies global nonnegativity even where the denominator vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D,f,p_1,\ldots,p_r\in\mathbb R[x]\), with \(D\ne0\), satisfy \(D^2f=\sum_{j=1}^r p_j^2\) as a polynomial identity. Then \(f(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). The identity gives nonnegativity on \(\{D\ne0\}\), which is dense because \(D\) is not the zero polynomial, and continuity extends it to \(\{D=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero polynomial denominator may vanish, but the cleared SOS identity still certifies nonnegativity everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.

notation.meaning: Complement of the real zero set of the denominator polynomial.

review_flags: The denominator need not be nowhere zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Soundness at Zeros of a Common Denominator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of ordering-based interpretation when the coefficient field is not formally real.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a field with \(\operatorname{char}K\ne2\). If \(-1\in\Sigma K^2\), then every element of \(K\), and of every extension field of \(K\), is a sum of squares. In particular, \(K(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\Sigma K(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^2\), so rational-SOS membership carries no nontrivial ordering-based positivity information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over a non-formally-real coefficient field of characteristic not two, every rational function is a sum of squares, so rational-SOS membership no longer detects positivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\Sigma K(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^2\).

notation.meaning: Finite sums of squares of elements of the field.

knowledge_statements.title: Collapse over Nonreal Coefficient Fields

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a formally real field of characteristic different from \(2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in\Sigma K(x)^2\) exactly when \(f\) is nonnegative in every ordering of \(K(x)\).

notation.meaning: Rational function field over the coefficient field.
Cone of finite sums of squares in the rational function field.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the ordering-theoretic formulation valid over formally real coefficient fields.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.3 Uniform denominators p. 59

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a formally real coefficient field \(K\), a rational-sum-of-squares certificate over \(K\) is an identity \[f=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\left(\frac{p_j}{q_j}\right)^2\quad\text{in }K(x_1,\ldots,x_n),\] with \(p_j,q_j\in K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) and \(q_j\ne0\). Such an identity exists if and only if \(f\) is nonnegative in every ordering of the field \(K(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\). When \(K\) is real closed, this specializes to the usual Hilbert-seventeenth certificate for polynomials nonnegative on \(K^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coefficient field determines the positivity test: rational SOS over a formally real field corresponds to nonnegativity in every ordering of its rational function field.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Field Certificate Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.3 Uniform denominators p. 59

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(2d\) satisfying \(F(x)>0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\). Then there exists an integer \(r\ge0\) and homogeneous polynomials \(P_1,\ldots,P_s\) of degree \(d+r\) such that \[\bigl(x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2\bigr)^rF(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{s}P_j(x)^2.\] Thus a power of the canonical positive quadratic form supplies an explicit denominator family for rational-SOS representations of positive definite forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every positive definite even-degree form becomes a sum of squares after multiplication by a sufficiently high power of the squared Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Reznick Certificate Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes the theorem's strict hypothesis from mere nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reznick's completeness assertion assumes \(F(x)>0\) for every \(x\ne0\). If \(F\) is merely positive semidefinite and has a nonzero zero, the theorem does not guarantee a finite \(r\) with \(\rho^rF\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\). Membership may still hold for particular semidefinite forms, but requires a separate argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reznick's theorem guarantees finite norm-power certificates for positive-definite forms, not for every nonnegative form with zeros.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonnegative form that may vanish away from the origin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted Reznick theorem alone does not imply \(F\in\bigcup_{r\ge0}\mathcal R_r\).

notation.meaning: Forms whose product with the r-th norm power is SOS.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested Reznick Cones and Reznick Index
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Organizes norm-power certificates by multiplier exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For forms of degree \(2d\), define \[\mathcal R_r=\{F:\rho^rF\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\},\qquad \rho=x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2.\] These cones are nested: \(\mathcal R_r\subseteq\mathcal R_{r+1}\). For \(F\in\bigcup_{r\ge0}\mathcal R_r\), define \[r_R(F)=\min\{r\ge0:F\in\mathcal R_r\}.\] At fixed \(r\), membership is equivalent to positive-semidefinite Gram feasibility for \(\rho^rF\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reznick certificates form nested cones; the least successful multiplier exponent is the Reznick index, and each fixed level is an SOS Gram test.

For every integer \(r\ge0\) satisfying \[r\ge \frac{n d(d-1)}{4(\log 2)\varepsilon(F)}-\frac{n+2d}{2},\] one has \(\rho^rF\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2\), where \(\rho=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite form has an explicit sufficient Reznick exponent controlled by its degree, dimension, and spherical minimum-to-maximum ratio.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Denominators Can Hide Negative Projective Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows why a denominator-SOS identity must control the real zeros of its denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=(x_0x_1)\subset\mathbb R[x_0,x_1]\), \(X=V_{\mathbb P}(I)\), \(Q=x_0\), and \(F=x_0^2-x_1^2\). Then \[Q^2F\equiv(x_0^2)^2\pmod I,\] while \(F([0:1])=-1\). Thus a congruence \(Q^2F\equiv\sum_jP_j^2\pmod I\) need not certify points of \(X(\mathbb R)\) where \(Q\) vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous denominator-SOS identity can conceal a negative value at a projective zero of the denominator.

A projective nonnegativity certificate for a form \(F\) of degree \(2d\) consists of a form \(Q\) of degree \(e\) and forms \(P_1,\ldots,P_s\) of degree \(d+e\) satisfying \[Q^2F-\sum_{j=1}^{s}P_j^2\in I.\] If \(Q(\xi)\ne0\) for every \(\xi\in X(\mathbb R)\), evaluation of the identity at real projective points certifies that \(F(\xi)\ge0\) on \(X(\mathbb R)\).

children.title: Polynomial Homogenization
children.top_down_role: Homogeneous reformulations used to transfer positivity questions into projective settings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The graded multiplicative law used when transporting polynomial identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\ge\deg f\) and \(e\ge\deg g\), prescribed-degree homogenization satisfies \[(fg)^h_{d+e}=f^h_dg^h_e.\] In particular, \((p^2)^h_{2d}=(p^h_d)^2\) whenever \(d\ge\deg p\). Consequently, an identity can be homogenized consistently by assigning compatible prescribed degrees and bringing all summands to a common total degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization is multiplicative when prescribed degrees are added, allowing certificate identities to be homogenized consistently.

notation.meaning: Homogenization of f to prescribed degree d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-aware homogenization with a designated homogenizing coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The degree-\(d\) homogenization of \(f\) is the form \[f^h(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n)=x_0^d f\!\left(\frac{x_1}{x_0},\ldots,\frac{x_n}{x_0}\right)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le d}c_\alpha x_0^{d-|\alpha|}x^\alpha.\] It is homogeneous of degree \(d\), restricts to \(f\) on the affine chart \(x_0=1\), and satisfies \(f^h(0,x)=f_d(x)\), where \(f_d\) is the degree-\(d\) homogeneous component of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization adds a coordinate so every monomial has the same chosen degree, recovers the polynomial on the affine chart, and exposes its leading form at infinity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes real points of the algebraic projective closure from limits of unbounded real affine points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subset\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb R}\) be defined by \(x^2+y^4=0\). Its real affine locus is only \((0,0)\), but its projective closure \[x^2x_0^2+y^4=0\] contains the real point \([0:1:0]\) on \(x_0=0\). Hence a real point of the algebraic projective boundary need not be approached by an unbounded sequence of real affine points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coercivity Does Not Require a Positive-Definite Leading Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates strict leading-form positivity from coercivity itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polynomial \[f(x,y)=x^4+y^2\] is coercive, but its degree-four leading form is \(f_4(x,y)=x^4\), which vanishes at the nonzero directions \((0,\pm1)\). Thus positive definiteness of the leading form is sufficient, but not necessary, for coercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coercive polynomial x⁴+y² has a leading form that vanishes in the y-direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is coercive while \(f_4(0,1)=0\).

notation.meaning: Degree-four leading homogeneous part of f.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f_{2d}>0\) on the unit sphere, then \(f(x)\to+\infty\) as \(\|x\|\to\infty\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained strict positivity at infinity and its coercivity consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polynomial \(f\) is strictly positive at infinity when \[f^h(0,u)=f_{2d}(u)>0\qquad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb R^n\text{ with }\|u\|=1.\] Compactness of the unit sphere then gives a constant \(c>0\) such that \(f_{2d}(u)\ge c\) there. Consequently, \(f(x)=\|x\|^{2d}f_{2d}(x/\|x\|)+O(\|x\|^{2d-1})\) and hence \(f(x)\to+\infty\) as \(\|x\|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity of an even-degree leading form in every direction is positivity on the projective boundary and implies coercivity of the polynomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Positivity at Infinity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(H=\sum_{j=1}^{s}P_j^2\) with each \(P_j\) homogeneous of degree \(d\), then dehomogenization gives \[H(1,x)=\sum_{j=1}^{s}P_j(1,x)^2.\] Conversely, if \(f=\sum_{j=1}^{s}p_j^2\), \(\deg f\le2d\), and \(\deg p_j\le d\), then degree-\(2d\) homogenization gives \[f^h_{2d}=\sum_{j=1}^{s}\left(x_0^d p_j(x/x_0)\right)^2.\] Rehomogenizing with the actual degree of \(H(1,x)\), rather than the prescribed degree \(2d\), can lose powers of \(x_0\) and therefore discard information at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS identities survive dehomogenization and degree-aware rehomogenization, but forgetting the original degree can erase factors and geometric information at infinity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Krivine–Stengle Nonnegativity, Positivity, and Vanishing Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preordering certificates on a basic closed semialgebraic set over a real closed field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\) be a real closed field, let \(p\in k[\mathbf{x}]\), and set \(K=\{\mathbf{x}\in k^n:f_j(\mathbf{x})\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), with \(P=P(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\). Then: (a) \(p\ge0\) on \(K\) if and only if there exist \(\ell\in\mathbb N\) and \(g,h\in P\) such that \(pg=p^{2\ell}+h\); (b) \(p>0\) on \(K\) if and only if there exist \(g,h\in P\) such that \(pg=1+h\); and (c) \(p=0\) on \(K\) if and only if there exist \(\ell\in\mathbb N\) and \(g\in P\) such that \(p^{2\ell}+g=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a basic closed semialgebraic set over a real closed field, nonnegativity, strict positivity, and identically vanishing are respectively equivalent to the stated preordering identities.
assumptions_latex: k\text{ is a real closed field}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}p\ge0\text{ on }K&\iff\exists\ell\in\mathbb N,\ g,h\in P:\ pg=p^{2\ell}+h,\\p>0\text{ on }K&\iff\exists g,h\in P:\ pg=1+h,\\p=0\text{ on }K&\iff\exists\ell\in\mathbb N,\ g\in P:\ p^{2\ell}+g=0.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preordering encoding of polynomial weak inequalities in the Krivine–Stengle framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For polynomials \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), the weak-inequality region is \[K_g=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge 0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Its generated preordering is \[T(g)=\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots g_m^{\alpha_m}:\sigma_\alpha\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.\] Every \(p\in T(g)\) satisfies \(p(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in K_g\); products indexed by \(\alpha\) encode all interactions among the weak inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Disequality-Monoid Encoding
Disequality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative-monoid encoding of polynomial disequalities in Stengle-type certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For polynomials \(d_1,\ldots,d_r\in\mathbb R[x]\), the disequality region is \[D=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:d_j(x)\ne0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,r\}.\] Let \[M(d)=\{d_1^{\beta_1}\cdots d_r^{\beta_r}:\beta\in\mathbb N^r\}.\] Every \(q\in M(d)\) is nonzero on \(D\), and hence \(q^2>0\) there. Thus a squared monoid element supplies the strictly positive term associated with disequalities in a Krivine–Stengle infeasibility identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disequalities generate a multiplicative monoid; squaring any monoid element gives a strictly positive term wherever all disequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in D,\ q\in M(d)\Longrightarrow q(x)^2>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sign Interaction of Mixed Certificate Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise interaction of preordering, ideal, and disequality-monoid components on a mixed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[S=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0,\ h_j(x)=0,\ d_k(x)\ne0\}.\] For \(p\in T(g)\), \(q\in M(d)\), and \(u\in I(h)\), every \(x\in S\) satisfies \[p(x)\ge0,\qquad q(x)^2>0,\qquad u(x)=0,\] and therefore \(p(x)+q(x)^2+u(x)>0\). Consequently, a polynomial identity \(p+q^2+u=0\) is incompatible with the existence of a point in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a mixed feasible set, the preordering term is nonnegative, the squared disequality term is positive, and the ideal term vanishes; hence a zero-sum identity certifies emptiness.
assumptions_latex: All constraint polynomials belong to \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p+q^2+u=0\Longrightarrow S=\varnothing.

Mixed Constraint Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krivine–Stengle emptiness identity for simultaneous inequalities, equalities, and disequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ h_j(x)=0,\ d_k(x)\ne0\text{ for all }i,j,k\}.\] Write \(T(g)\) for the preordering generated by the \(g_i\), \(I(h)\) for the ideal generated by the \(h_j\), and \(M(d)\) for the multiplicative monoid generated by the \(d_k\). Then \(S=\varnothing\) if and only if there exist \(p\in T(g)\), \(q\in M(d)\), and \(u\in I(h)\) satisfying \[p+q^2+u=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed basic semialgebraic set is empty exactly when preordering, monoid-square, and ideal terms sum identically to zero.
assumptions_latex: All constraint polynomials belong to \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\varnothing\Longleftrightarrow\exists p\in T(g),\ q\in M(d),\ u\in I(h):p+q^2+u=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constructive Schmüdgen Certificate Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-indexed finite-dimensional families of Schmüdgen preordering representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each integer \(d\ge0\), define \[T_d(g)=\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g^\alpha:\sigma_\alpha\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_\alpha g^\alpha)\le2d\right\}.\] Membership in \(T_d(g)\) is representable by finitely many positive-semidefinite Gram matrices. The family is nested, \(T_d(g)\subseteq T_{d+1}(g)\), and \(T(g)=\bigcup_{d\ge0}T_d(g)\). Consequently, under Schmüdgen’s hypotheses, every polynomial strictly positive on \(K\) belongs to \(T_d(g)\) for some finite but generally unspecified \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degree truncations form nested semidefinite-representable certificate families, and every Schmüdgen certificate appears at some finite level.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\}\) is compact for the completeness conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(g)=\bigcup_{d\ge0}T_d(g)\) and \(f>0\text{ on }K\Longrightarrow\exists d:\ f\in T_d(g)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), let \[M(g)=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.\] The quadratic module \(M(g)\) is Archimedean if there exists \(N>0\) such that \[N-\sum_{j=1}^n x_j^2\in M(g).\] Equivalently, for every \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), there exists \(N_p>0\) such that \(N_p+p\in M(g)\) and \(N_p-p\in M(g)\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract Archimedean representation theorem for quadratic modules in commutative unital real algebras.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a commutative unital real algebra and \(M\subseteq A\) an Archimedean quadratic module. Set \[X_M=\{\varphi:A\to\mathbb R:\varphi\text{ is a unital algebra homomorphism and }\varphi(M)\subseteq\mathbb R_{\ge0}\}.\] If \(a\in A\) satisfies \(\varphi(a)>0\) for every \(\varphi\in X_M\), then \(a\in M\). For \(A=\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) and \(M=M(g)\), the characters are evaluations and \(X_M\) identifies with \(K_g\), giving the polynomial Putinar theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity on every character nonnegative on an Archimedean quadratic module implies membership in that module; the polynomial specialization is Putinar's theorem.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a commutative unital real algebra.
\(M\subseteq A\) is an Archimedean quadratic module.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_m\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real Nullstellensatz characterization of polynomials vanishing on a real variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ideal \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), \[\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}=I(V_{\mathbb R}(I))=\{f:f(x)=0\text{ for every }x\in V_{\mathbb R}(I)\}.\] A polynomial \(f\) belongs to \(\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}\) if and only if there exist \(r\ge1\) and \(\sigma\in\Sigma[x]\) such that \[f^{2r}+\sigma\in I.\] If \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_m\rangle\), this is certified by an identity \[f^{2r}+\sigma=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i h_i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial vanishes on a real variety exactly when an even power plus a sum of squares belongs to the defining ideal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}\Longleftrightarrow\exists r\ge1,\exists\sigma\in\Sigma[x]:f^{2r}+\sigma\in I\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) have degree \(n\). Second, setting \(g_1=1-x\), \(g_2=1+x\), and \(g_3=g_1g_2\), one has \(p\ge0\) on \([-1,1]\) if and only if \(p=f_0+g_1f_1+g_2f_2+g_3f_3\) for \(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3\in\Sigma[x]\). In the second representation every summand has degree at most \(n\); if \(n\) is even then \(f_1=f_2=0\), and if \(n\) is odd then \(f_0=f_3=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: An SOS optimality-gap representation induces KKT data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial optimization with inequalities $g_j\geq0$ and equalities $h_\ell=0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $x^*\in K$ be a global minimizer with value $f^*$. Suppose, identically on $\mathbb R^n$, that $f-f^*=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^{m_1}\sigma_jg_j+\sum_{\ell=1}^{m_2}\psi_\ell h_\ell$, where every $\sigma_j$ is SOS and every $\psi_\ell$ is a polynomial. Then $\sigma_0(x^*)=0$, $\sigma_j(x^*)\geq0$, $g_j(x^*)\geq0$, and $\sigma_j(x^*)g_j(x^*)=0$ for every $j$. Moreover, $
abla f(x^*)=\sum_j\sigma_j(x^*)
abla g_j(x^*)+\sum_\ell\psi_\ell(x^*)
abla h_\ell(x^*)$, so $(x^*,\lambda^*,v^*)$ is a KKT triplet with $\lambda_j^*=\sigma_j(x^*)$ and $v_\ell^*=\psi_\ell(x^*)$. Finally, $\mathcal L(x,\sigma,\psi)=f(x)-f^*-\sum_j\sigma_j(x)g_j(x)-\sum_\ell\psi_\ell(x)h_\ell(x)=\sigma_0(x)\geq0$, and $x^*$ is a global minimizer of $\mathcal L$ on $\mathbb R^n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOS-plus-constraint representation of the global optimality gap yields complementary nonnegative multipliers and the KKT stationarity equation at a global minimizer. The generalized Lagrangian equals the nonnegative SOS remainder and is globally minimized at that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\sigma_0(x^*)=0,\quad\sigma_j(x^*)g_j(x^*)=0,\quad 
abla f(x^*)=\sum_j\sigma_j(x^*)
abla g_j(x^*)+\sum_\ell\psi_\ell(x^*)
abla h_\ell(x^*),\quad x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\mathcal L(x,\sigma,\psi).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a quadratic module \(M\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) with positivity set \(K\), define its saturation by \(\operatorname{Sat}(M)=\{h\in\mathbb R[x]:h(x)\geq0\text{ for every }x\in K\}\). If \(M\) is archimedean and \(f\in\operatorname{Sat}(M)\) has finite zero set \(Z_K(f)\), then the local-global principle gives the finite-zero saturation criterion \(f\in M\) whenever \(f\in M\widehat{\mathcal O}_p\) for every \(p\in Z_K(f)\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\bigcup_{j=1}^r[a_j,b_j]\subseteq\mathbb R\), where \(a_1<b_1<a_2<\cdots<a_r<b_r\). Define \(g_0=x-a_1\), \(g_j=(x-a_{j+1})(x-b_j)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r-1\), and \(g_r=b_r-x\). The preordering \(T(g_0,\ldots,g_r)\) is saturated: every \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfying \(f\geq0\) on \(K\) has a representation \(f=\sum_{e\in\{0,1\}^{r+1}}\sigma_e\prod_{j=0}^r g_j^{e_j}\), where every \(\sigma_e\) is a sum of squares. Conversely, every such representation certifies \(f\geq0\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many disjoint closed intervals, every nonnegative polynomial belongs to the preordering generated by the natural endpoint and gap polynomials.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificates on Unions of Intervals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The natural generators have the correct sign on the interval union and the certificate fits the leaf, but the saturation theorem and its exact generator assumptions require a primary or authoritative source locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-degree lower-bound hierarchy generated by products of affine polytope inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:\ell_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), define \(H_d=\{\sum_{|\alpha|\le d}c_\alpha\ell^\alpha:c_\alpha\ge0\}\) and \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in H_d\}\), with \(\rho_d=-\infty\) if the feasible set is empty. If \(P\) is compact with nonempty interior, then \(\rho_d\le\rho_{d+1}\le\min_P f\) and \(\rho_d\to\min_P f\). Coefficient matching is a linear program with at most \(\binom{m+d}{d}\) nonnegative product coefficients, in addition to \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated Handelman cones give linear-programming lower bounds increasing to the polynomial minimum on a compact full-dimensional polytope.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a compact polytope with nonempty interior described by affine inequalities \(\ell_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d\uparrow\min_{x\in P}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Handelman Linear-Programming Hierarchy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the unmodified Handelman cone to capture general nonnegative polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=[-1,1]=\{x:x+1\ge0,\ 1-x\ge0\}\), the polynomial \(f(x)=x^2\) is nonnegative on \(P\) and vanishes at the interior point \(0\), but \(x^2\notin\operatorname{cone}\{(x+1)^p(1-x)^q:p,q\in\mathbb N\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative polynomial with an interior zero need not have a Handelman representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^2\notin\operatorname{cone}\{(x+1)^p(1-x)^q:p,q\in\mathbb N\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Interior Zeros Obstruct Handelman Representation

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_i(x)\geq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is a compact polytope with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha\prod_{i=1}^m\ell_i^{\alpha_i}\) for a finite \(A\subseteq\mathbb N^m\) and coefficients \(c_\alpha>0\).

notation.meaning: Compact polytope described by affine inequalities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-positivity Handelman theorem for full-dimensional compact polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_i(x)\geq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be a compact polytope with nonempty interior, where the \(\ell_i\) are affine linear. If \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) is strictly positive on \(P\), then there exist a finite set \(A\subseteq\mathbb N^m\) and coefficients \(c_\alpha>0\) such that \(f=\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha\prod_{i=1}^m\ell_i^{\alpha_i}\). Each summand is nonnegative on \(P\), so the identity is a directly checkable positivity certificate. Nonnegativity without strict positivity is not covered in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every polynomial strictly positive on a compact full-dimensional polytope is a positive linear combination of finite products of its defining affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Handelman Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-positivity Handelman certificate fits the leaf, but the exact hypotheses on the affine description require a source. The sentence justifying nonnegativity of each summand is proof-style text.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pólya Coefficient Hierarchy for Simplex Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficientwise hierarchy for minimizing a homogeneous polynomial on the standard simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be homogeneous of degree \(d\), let \(s=x_1+\cdots+x_n\), and define \(\rho_r=\sup\{\gamma:\text{every coefficient of }s^r(f-\gamma s^d)\text{ is nonnegative}\}\). Then \(\rho_r\le\rho_{r+1}\le\min_{\Delta_{n-1}}f\) and \(\rho_r\to\min_{\Delta_{n-1}}f\). Level \(r\) tests \(\binom{n+d+r-1}{d+r}\) coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive coordinate-sum multipliers give coefficientwise lower bounds converging to the simplex minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r\uparrow\min_{x\in\Delta_{n-1}}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Pólya Coefficient Hierarchy for Simplex Lower Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard sufficient exponent bound for coefficient positivity on the simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}c_\alpha x^\alpha\) be homogeneous of degree \(d\), positive on \(\Delta_{n-1}\), and define \(\lambda=\min_{\Delta_{n-1}}f\) and \(L=\max_{|\alpha|=d}|c_\alpha|\alpha!/d!\). Every integer \(r\) satisfying \(r>\frac{d(d-1)}{2}\frac{L}{\lambda}-d\) is sufficient for all coefficients of \((x_1+\cdots+x_n)^r f\) to be positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive margin and normalized coefficient size give an explicit sufficient Pólya exponent.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is homogeneous of degree \(d\) and strictly positive on \(\Delta_{n-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r>\frac{d(d-1)}{2}\frac{L}{\lambda}-d\Longrightarrow (x_1+\cdots+x_n)^rf\text{ has positive coefficients}.\)

notation.meaning: Positive minimum of f on the simplex

knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Pólya Exponent Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-positivity boundary for the unperturbed Pólya family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x_1,x_2)=(x_1-x_2)^2\), one has \(f\ge0\) on \(\Delta_1\) and \(f(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)=0\), while for every \(r\in\mathbb N\), \((x_1+x_2)^rf\) has at least one negative coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative simplex polynomial with an interior zero can fail every unperturbed Pólya coefficient test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall r\in\mathbb N\), \((x_1+x_2)^rf\) is not coefficientwise nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Zeros Prevent Coefficientwise Pólya Certificates

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some \(r\in\mathbb N\), every coefficient of \((x_1+\cdots+x_n)^r f\) is strictly positive.

notation.meaning: Homogeneous polynomial strictly positive on the simplex

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical homogeneous Pólya certificate on the standard simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be homogeneous and strictly positive on the standard simplex \(\Delta_{n-1}=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:x_1+\cdots+x_n=1\}\). Then there exists \(r\in\mathbb N\) such that every monomial coefficient of \((x_1+\cdots+x_n)^r f\) is strictly positive. Because \(x_1+\cdots+x_n=1\) on \(\Delta_{n-1}\), the coefficient-positive polynomial equals \(f\) there and provides a finite positivity certificate. Strict positivity, rather than mere nonnegativity, is essential to this conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous polynomial strictly positive on the simplex becomes coefficientwise positive after multiplication by a sufficiently high power of the coordinate sum.
knowledge_statements.title: Pólya Certificate Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The homogeneous strict-positivity statement and certificate kind fit the Pólya leaf, but no authoritative locator is supplied. The explanatory simplex-equality argument is proof-style text.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite range and sign test for a polynomial in a fixed-degree simplex Bernstein basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f=\sum_{|\alpha|=m}b_\alpha B_\alpha^{(m)}\) on \(\Delta_{n-1}\), then \(\min_{|\alpha|=m}b_\alpha\le f(x)\le\max_{|\alpha|=m}b_\alpha\) for every \(x\in\Delta_{n-1}\). Thus nonnegative coefficients certify \(f\ge0\), and positive coefficients certify \(f>0\), on the simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest and largest Bernstein coefficients enclose the polynomial's range, so coefficient signs certify positivity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is expressed in the degree-\(m\) Bernstein basis on \(\Delta_{n-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_\alpha b_\alpha\le f(x)\le\max_\alpha b_\alpha\) on \(\Delta_{n-1}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Bernstein Coefficient Range Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavior of simplex Bernstein range bounds under repeated degree elevation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed polynomial \(f\) on \(\Delta_{n-1}\), let \(L_m=\min_{|\alpha|=m}b_\alpha^{(m)}\) and \(U_m=\max_{|\alpha|=m}b_\alpha^{(m)}\). For \(m\ge\deg f\), \(L_m\le L_{m+1}\le\min_{\Delta_{n-1}}f\) and \(\max_{\Delta_{n-1}}f\le U_{m+1}\le U_m\), with \(L_m\to\min_{\Delta_{n-1}}f\) and \(U_m\to\max_{\Delta_{n-1}}f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degree elevation monotonically tightens Bernstein coefficient bounds, which converge to the true simplex range.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a fixed polynomial on the standard simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_m\uparrow\min_{\Delta_{n-1}}f\) and \(U_m\downarrow\max_{\Delta_{n-1}}f\).

notation.meaning: Minimum and maximum degree-m Bernstein coefficients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-elevated Bernstein certificate for strict positivity on a simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be a polynomial on \(\Delta_{n-1}=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:\sum_i x_i=1\}\), and assume \(f>0\) on \(\Delta_{n-1}\). For every sufficiently large \(m\geq\deg f\), degree elevation gives \(f=\sum_{|\alpha|=m}b_\alpha^{(m)}B_\alpha^{(m)}\), where \(B_\alpha^{(m)}(x)=\frac{m!}{\alpha_1!\cdots\alpha_n!}x^\alpha\), and all coefficients satisfy \(b_\alpha^{(m)}>0\). Since \(B_\alpha^{(m)}\geq0\) and \(\sum_{|\alpha|=m}B_\alpha^{(m)}=1\) on the simplex, coefficient positivity certifies \(f>0\) there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial strictly positive on a simplex has only positive Bernstein coefficients after sufficiently many degree elevations, which directly certifies positivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Bernstein-Basis Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projectively compactified weighted-SOS version for noncompact basic closed sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\geq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be possibly noncompact. Assume the compatible homogenizations of the constraints generate an archimedean quadratic module on the compact projective closure of \(K\), and assume an even-degree homogenization of \(f\) is strictly positive on that closure, including its points at infinity. Then there exist \(r\in\mathbb N\) and sums of squares \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\mathbb R[x]\) such that \((1+\|x\|^2)^r f=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i\). The weight clears the projective denominator and yields a verifiable certificate on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict positivity on a suitable projective compactification, a polynomial on a noncompact semialgebraic set has a weighted quadratic-module SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Putinar–Vasilescu Certificate Family

children.title: Coercive Positivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Noncompact positivity settings controlled by coercive behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard sufficient, but not necessary, algebraic condition for global coercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) have even degree \(2d\), with leading homogeneous form \(f_{2d}\). If \(f_{2d}(u)>0\) for every \(u\ne0\), equivalently \(\min_{u\in\mathbb S^{n-1}}f_{2d}(u)>0\), then \(f(x)\to+\infty\) as \(\|x\|\to\infty\). If additionally \(f>0\), then \(f\) attains a strictly positive global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite leading form makes an even-degree polynomial coercive and, with strict positivity, gives an attained positive minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)\to+\infty\text{ as }\|x\|\to\infty.

notation.meaning: leading homogeneous component of the polynomial

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Leading-Form Criterion

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is coercive on }K\Longleftrightarrow\lim_{r\to\infty}\inf\{f(x):x\in K,\ \|x\|\ge r\}=+\infty\).

notation.meaning: Infimum of the objective over the portion of the feasible set outside the radius-\(r\) ball.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent escaping-infimum formulation of coercivity relative to a feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\). With \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), define \(\rho(r)=\inf\{f(x):x\in K,\ \|x\|\ge r\}\). Then \(f\) is coercive on \(K\) if and only if \(\rho(r)\to+\infty\) as \(r\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative coercivity is equivalent to the infimum outside each growing ball tending to positive infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Escaping-Infimum Characterization of Relative Coercivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Radial Growth Lower Bound Certifies Relative Coercivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A directly checkable sufficient growth condition on a possibly noncompact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(f:K\to\mathbb R\). If there exist \(a>0\), \(q>0\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(R\ge0\) such that \(f(x)\ge a\|x\|^q-b\) for every \(x\in K\) with \(\|x\|\ge R\), then \(f\) is coercive on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-power radial lower bound outside a ball certifies coercive growth relative to the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The radial lower bound holds for every feasible point outside a fixed ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x_k\|\to\infty,\ x_k\in K\Longrightarrow f(x_k)\to+\infty.
review_flags: The condition is sufficient, not necessary.
knowledge_statements.title: Radial Growth Lower Bound Certifies Relative Coercivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary Leading-Form Conditions for Polynomial Coercivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary asymptotic restrictions on a globally coercive nonconstant polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) be nonconstant and coercive on \(\mathbb R^n\), and let \(f_d\) be its leading homogeneous form. Then \(d\) is even and \(f_d(u)\ge0\) for every \(u\). Positive definiteness of \(f_d\) is sufficient but not necessary for coercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive polynomial has even degree and a nonnegative leading form, which may vanish in some directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\in2\mathbb N,\qquad f_d(u)\ge0\quad\forall u\in\mathbb R^n.
review_flags: Leading-form nonnegativity is necessary but not sufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Necessary Leading-Form Conditions for Polynomial Coercivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Coercivity, Compact Sublevels, and Positive Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational coercive positivity regime on a closed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed and let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. Then \(f(x_k)\to+\infty\) for every sequence \(x_k\in K\) with \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\) if and only if every sublevel set \(\{x\in K:f(x)\le c\}\) is compact. In this regime \(f\) attains its minimum; if additionally \(f>0\) on \(K\), the attained minimum is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous function on a nonempty closed set, relative coercivity is equivalent to compact sublevels and ensures attainment; strict positivity then yields a positive margin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ coercive on }K\Longleftrightarrow\{x\in K:f(x)\le c\}\text{ compact for all }c;\quad f>0\Longrightarrow\min_K f>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Coercivity, Compact Sublevels, and Positive Attainment

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in K}f(x)>0\), and the minimum is attained.

notation.meaning: nonempty closed basic semialgebraic feasible set
polynomial whose positivity and coercivity are considered

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: for a continuous function on a nonempty closed subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space, coercivity is equivalent to compactness of all sublevel sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A noncompact positivity regime combining strict positivity with growth at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\). The pair \((f,K)\) is in the coercive positivity regime when \(f(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\) and \(f\) is coercive on \(K\), meaning \(f(x_k)\to+\infty\) for every sequence \((x_k)\subset K\) with \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\). Equivalently, every sublevel set \(\{x\in K:f(x)\le c\}\) is compact. Consequently, \(f\) attains a strictly positive minimum on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nonempty closed feasible set, strict positivity together with coercive growth, equivalently compactness of every sublevel set, implies attainment of a strictly positive minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercive Positivity Regimes

children.title: Weighted Certificate Families
