knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Certificate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Denominator-free weighted quadratic-module certificates indexed by a coercive polynomial weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(M(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\in\Sigma[x]\}\). Fix a polynomial weight \(\theta\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfying \(\theta(x)>0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), typically \(\theta(x)=1+\|x\|^2\). The weighted certificate family generated by \(M(g)\) and \(\theta\) is \(C_\theta(M(g))=\{f\in\mathbb R[x]:\theta^rf\in M(g)\text{ for some }r\in\mathbb N\}\). Membership supplies an SOS identity and therefore certifies \(f\ge0\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial has a weighted certificate when multiplication by some power of a positive coercive weight places it in the quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in C_\theta(M(g))\Longrightarrow f(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Growth-Controlled Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational SOS representations whose denominator is a prescribed positive growth weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(g)\) be the quadratic module of a basic closed set \(K\), and let \(\theta>0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). A growth-controlled representation of \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) is an identity \[f=\frac{\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j}{\theta^r},\qquad \sigma_j\in\Sigma[x],\quad r\in\mathbb N.\] Equivalently, \(\theta^rf=\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jg_j\). The exponent \(r\) controls the allowed denominator growth, while positivity of \(\theta\) makes the quotient everywhere defined and ensures that the representation certifies \(f\ge0\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polynomial is represented by a quadratic-module numerator divided by a controlled power of an everywhere-positive weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta^rf\in M(g)\Longleftrightarrow f=\theta^{-r}(\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jg_j)\), which implies \(f\ge0\) on \(K\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that coercivity is sufficient but not necessary for an attained strictly positive minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x,y)=1+x^2y^2\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), \(f\ge1\), and the minimum \(1\) is attained whenever \(xy=0\). Nevertheless \(f(0,t)=1\) for every \(t\), so \(f\) is not coercive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polynomial one plus x-squared y-squared has an attained positive minimum but is noncoercive along an unbounded coordinate axis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2}f(x,y)=1\text{ is attained, but }f\text{ is not coercive}.

notation.meaning: positive noncoercive polynomial with an unbounded minimum set

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Minimum Without Coercivity

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is coercive},\quad g\text{ is not coercive},\quad f_4=g_4=x^4\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Degree-four leading homogeneous forms of the two polynomials.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two polynomials with the same semidefinite leading form but opposite coercivity behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polynomials \(f(x,y)=x^4+y^2\) and \(g(x,y)=x^4+1\) have the same degree-four leading form \(x^4\), which is nonnegative but not positive definite. Nevertheless, \(f\) is coercive on \(\mathbb R^2\), whereas \(g(0,t)=1\) for every \(t\), so \(g\) is not coercive. Semidefiniteness of the leading form alone therefore neither proves nor disproves coercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative but non-positive-definite leading form cannot decide coercivity because lower-degree growth along its zero directions is decisive.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semidefinite Leading Form Is Inconclusive for Coercivity
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Leading Form Is Inconclusive for Coercivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coercivity Without a Strict Positive Margin
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that coercivity controls escape to infinity but does not itself imply strict positivity or a positive minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=x^2\) on \(K=\mathbb R\), one has \(f(x)\to+\infty\) as \(|x|\to\infty\), so \(f\) is coercive. Nevertheless, \(f(0)=0\), and hence \(\min_{x\in K}f(x)=0\). Thus coercivity alone does not imply strict positivity or a strictly positive minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coercive polynomial x squared has minimum zero, so coercivity alone supplies no strict positive margin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is coercive on }\mathbb R,\qquad \min_{x\in\mathbb R}f(x)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity Without a Strict Positive Margin

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness Is Required for Coercive Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of coercive attainment on a nonclosed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=(0,1)\subset\mathbb R\) and \(f(x)=x^2\). There is no sequence in \(K\) whose norm tends to infinity, so the escaping-sequence definition of coercivity holds vacuously. Nevertheless, \(\inf_{x\in K}f(x)=0\), and the infimum is not attained. Thus escaping-sequence coercivity does not imply attainment without an additional closedness or compact-sublevel hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the nonclosed bounded set \((0,1)\), coercivity is vacuous while the infimum of \(x^2\) is unattained.
assumptions_latex: Coercivity is interpreted through escaping feasible sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is vacuously coercive on }K,\qquad \inf_K f=0\text{ is not attained}.
review_flags: The example also shows why compact-sublevel equivalence requires suitable closedness and lower-semicontinuity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Closedness Is Required for Coercive Attainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Positivity Without a Positive Attained Margin
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical failure of positive attainment when coercivity is absent on a noncompact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(f(x,y)=(xy-1)^2+x^2\). Then \(f(x,y)>0\) at every finite point, but \(f(t^{-1},t)=t^{-2}\to0\). Hence \(f\) is noncoercive, \(\inf f=0\), and the infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive noncoercive polynomial can approach zero along an escaping sequence and have no positive attained margin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f>0,\qquad \inf_{\mathbb R^2}f=0\text{ is not attained},\qquad f\text{ is not coercive}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Positivity Without a Positive Attained Margin
Coercivity Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict positivity without coercivity need not yield a positive attained minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(K=\mathbb R^2\), consider \(f(x,y)=(xy-1)^2+x^2\). One has \(f(x,y)>0\) at every finite point: equality would require simultaneously \(x=0\) and \(xy=1\), which is impossible. Nevertheless, along \((x,y)=(t^{-1},t)\) with \(t\to\infty\), one has \(f(t^{-1},t)=t^{-2}\to0\). Thus \(f\) is not coercive, \(\inf_K f=0\), and the infimum is not attained. Strict positivity alone therefore cannot provide the positive margin used by coercive certificate regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive polynomial on a noncompact set can approach zero at infinity when coercivity is absent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f>0\) on \(K\), but \(\inf_K f=0\) is not attained and \(f\) is not coercive.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificates on Cylindrical Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-module certificates for compact-base cylinders with unrestricted variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) and form the cylinder \(K=S\times\mathbb R^q\). For \(f\in\mathbb R[x,y]\), a cylindrical quadratic-module certificate is an identity \[f(x,y)=\sigma_0(x,y)+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(x,y)g_j(x),\qquad \sigma_j\in\Sigma[x,y].\] Because each multiplier is nonnegative and the generators constrain only the base variable \(x\), the identity is finitely verifiable and certifies \(f(x,y)\ge0\) for all \((x,y)\in S\times\mathbb R^q\). It is sufficient, not necessary in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS multipliers in all variables combined with base constraints certify nonnegativity throughout an unbounded cylinder.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jg_j\Longrightarrow f\ge0\) on \(S\times\mathbb R^q\).

For this point base the seeded cylindrical module reduces to \(\Sigma[u,v]\), so \(p\) has no certificate of that form.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\ge0\text{ on }S\times\mathbb R^2,\qquad p\notin\Sigma[u,v].

knowledge_statements.title: Cylindrical Certificate Nonnecessity
Certificates at Infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous certificates that include limiting directions on a projective or spherical compactification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) have even degree \(2d\), and define its homogenization by \(F(x_0,x)=x_0^{2d}f(x/x_0)\). Homogenize the constraint polynomials compatibly to obtain \(G_j\), and let \(K^h\) be the corresponding homogeneous feasible cone intersected with \(x_0^2+\|x\|^2=1\) and \(x_0\ge0\). An SOS identity \[F=\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jG_j+\tau(1-x_0^2-\|x\|^2)\] with homogeneous degree matching and \(\sigma_j\) SOS certifies nonnegativity both at finite points and at infinity, the latter represented by \(x_0=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization turns directions at infinity into boundary points where a degree-matched SOS identity can certify nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed identity implies \(F\ge0\) on \(K^h\), including its slice \(x_0=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Certificates on Affine Real Varieties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOS certificates modulo the vanishing ideal of an affine real variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_{\mathbb R}(h)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_i(x)=0,\ i=1,\ldots,s\}\) and \(K=V_{\mathbb R}(h)\cap\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). A quadratic-module certificate modulo the variety ideal is an identity \[f=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j+\sum_{i=1}^s\tau_i h_i,\qquad \sigma_j\in\Sigma[x],\quad \tau_i\in\mathbb R[x].\] On \(K\), the ideal terms vanish and every remaining term is nonnegative. Hence the identity is a finite algebraic certificate that \(f\ge0\) on the constrained real variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOS quadratic-module identity modulo the equality ideal certifies nonnegativity on the associated constrained real variety.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in M(g)+I(h)\Longrightarrow f(x)\ge0\) for all \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Certificates on Real Algebraic Curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preordering certificates modulo a curve ideal, including products of inequality generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=V_{\mathbb R}(I)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be an affine real algebraic curve and let \(K=C\cap\{g_1\ge0,\ldots,g_m\ge0\}\). A preordering certificate for \(f\) on \(K\) is an identity \[f=\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots g_m^{\alpha_m}+q,\qquad \sigma_\alpha\in\Sigma[x],\quad q\in I.\] Every generator product is nonnegative on \(K\), and \(q\) vanishes on \(C\); consequently, the identity certifies \(f\ge0\) on the curve segment \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a constrained real curve, SOS-weighted products of inequalities certify nonnegativity modulo the curve’s defining ideal.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) defines an affine real curve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in T(g)+I\Longrightarrow f\ge0\) on \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Nonsingular Curve Saturation
Dimension-Dependent Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOS saturation already separates univariate from bivariate polynomial rings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the unconstrained line, every polynomial \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfying \(p(x)\ge0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R\) is a sum of squares in \(\mathbb R[x]\); thus the SOS cone is saturated. This fails in dimension two: the Motzkin polynomial \[M(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4+1-3x^2y^2\] is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^2\) but is not a sum of squares of polynomials. Hence saturation of an algebraic certificate cone depends on dimension and cannot be inferred from its one-dimensional behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Univariate nonnegative polynomials are SOS, whereas the nonnegative Motzkin polynomial shows that unconstrained SOS saturation fails in two dimensions.
assumptions_latex: Saturation means equality between the certificate cone and all polynomials nonnegative on the domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Pos}(\mathbb R)=\Sigma[x]\), while \(\operatorname{Pos}(\mathbb R^2)\supsetneq\Sigma[x,y]\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm and SOS property of a symmetric matrix polynomial
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for real symmetric matrix-valued polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real symmetric \(\mathbf F\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]^{p\times p}\), define \(\|\mathbf F\|:=\sup_{\|\xi\|=1}\|\xi^T\mathbf F(\mathbf x)\xi\|_0\). The matrix polynomial \(\mathbf F\) is SOS if there exist \(q\in\mathbb N\) and \(\mathbf L\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]^{p\times q}\) such that \(\mathbf F=\mathbf L\mathbf L^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matrix-polynomial norm is the supremum over unit vectors of the scalar-polynomial norm of the associated quadratic form. A symmetric matrix polynomial is SOS exactly when it factors as a polynomial matrix times its transpose.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\mathbf F\|=\sup_{\|\xi\|=1}\|\xi^T\mathbf F(\mathbf x)\xi\|_0,\qquad \mathbf F\text{ is SOS}\iff\exists q\in\mathbb N,\ \exists\mathbf L\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]^{p\times q}:\mathbf F=\mathbf L\mathbf L^T

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Sum-of-Squares Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gram-factor certificates for positive-semidefinite symmetric matrix polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric matrix polynomial \(F\in\mathbb S^r[x]\) is a matrix sum of squares when there exist polynomial matrices \(H_1,\ldots,H_N\), each with \(r\) columns, such that \[F(x)=\sum_{k=1}^N H_k(x)^{\mathsf T}H_k(x).\] Equivalently, after choosing a monomial vector \(v_d(x)\), one may write \(F(x)=(v_d(x)\otimes I_r)^{\mathsf T}Q(v_d(x)\otimes I_r)\) for some constant matrix \(Q\succeq0\). Either representation is finitely verifiable and certifies \(F(x)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factoring a symmetric matrix polynomial as polynomial matrix squares certifies global positive semidefiniteness.
assumptions_latex: The factor matrices have polynomial entries and \(r\) columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\sum_kH_k^{\mathsf T}H_k\Longrightarrow F(x)\succeq0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: vector of monomials of degree at most d

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Non-Matrix-SOS Example
Scherer–Hol Certificate Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix quadratic-module certificates generated by symmetric polynomial matrix inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_j\in\mathbb S^{s_j}[x]\) define \(K=\{x:G_j(x)\succeq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). The Scherer–Hol matrix quadratic-module family consists of symmetric matrix polynomials admitting \[F=S_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sum_{k=1}^{N_j}A_{jk}^{\mathsf T}G_jA_{jk},\] where \(S_0\) is a matrix sum of squares and each \(A_{jk}\) is a polynomial matrix of compatible size. Every summand is positive semidefinite on \(K\), so this identity is a directly verifiable certificate that \(F(x)\succeq0\) throughout the matrix-defined feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial matrix congruences of the defining matrix inequalities, plus a matrix SOS term, certify matrix positivity on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in M^r(G)\Longrightarrow F(x)\succeq0\) for all \(x\in K\).

notation.meaning: r-by-r matrix quadratic module generated by the matrix constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Putinar Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedean matrix Putinar theorem for scalar polynomial inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and suppose the scalar quadratic module \(M(g)\) is Archimedean. If \(F\in\mathbb S^r[x]\) is strictly positive definite on \(K\), then there exist matrix sums of squares \(S_0,S_1,\ldots,S_m\in\mathbb S^r[x]\) such that \[F=S_0+\sum_{j=1}^m g_jS_j.\] Thus uniform matrix positivity over an Archimedean basic closed set has a finite matrix-SOS certificate in the matrix quadratic module generated by the scalar constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an Archimedean constraint module, every strictly positive-definite matrix polynomial has a matrix Putinar SOS representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in M^r(g)=\{S_0+\sum_{j=1}^mg_jS_j:S_j\text{ are matrix sums of squares}\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Archimedeanity does not in general make a quadratic module saturated: there exist Archimedean finitely generated modules \(M(g)\) and \(f\ge0\) on \(K=\{g_j\ge0\}\) with \(f\notin M(g)\). Hence \(F=[f]\), or \(F=\operatorname{diag}(f,1,\ldots,1)\), is positive semidefinite on \(K\) but need not belong to \(M^r(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archimedeanity alone does not permit strict positive definiteness in matrix Putinar's theorem to be replaced by positive semidefiniteness.
assumptions_latex: No saturation or additional boundary hypothesis is imposed.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Positivity Boundary for Matrix Putinar
Matrix Positivstellensatz with Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedean, strictly positive-definite matrix-polynomial version of Putinar's certificate and its auxiliary-vector lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(F\in\mathbb S^r[x]\). If the scalar quadratic module \(M(g)\) is Archimedean and \(F(x)\succ0\) for every \(x\in K\), then there are matrix sum-of-squares polynomials \(S_0,\ldots,S_m\in\mathbb S^r[x]\) such that
\[
F=S_0+\sum_{i=1}^m g_iS_i.
\]
More explicitly, for each \(i\) there are finitely many polynomial matrices \(H_{ij}\in\mathbb R[x]^{q_{ij}\times r}\) such that \(S_i=\sum_j H_{ij}^{\mathsf T}H_{ij}\). Introducing \(y\in\mathbb R^r\) gives the lifted scalar identity
\[
y^{\mathsf T}F(x)y=y^{\mathsf T}S_0(x)y+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x)y^{\mathsf T}S_i(x)y,
\]
where each \(y^{\mathsf T}S_i(x)y=\sum_j\lVert H_{ij}(x)y\rVert_2^2\) is a sum of squares in \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix polynomial that is strictly positive definite on an Archimedean basic closed set belongs to the corresponding matrix quadratic module; an auxiliary vector converts the matrix identity into a scalar SOS identity.
assumptions_latex: \(M(g)\) is the scalar quadratic module generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\), and \(M(g)\) is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=S_0+\sum_{i=1}^m g_iS_i\), where every \(S_i\) is a matrix sum of squares.

children.top_down_role: Algebraic decompositions induced by variable, support, or graph structure.

assumptions_latex: Each constraint index is assigned to a set \(J_k\), with \(g_j\in\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\) for \(j\in J_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\sum_{k=1}^s\left(\sigma_{0k}+\sum_{j\in J_k}\sigma_{jk}g_j\right)\) with \(\sigma_{0k},\sigma_{jk}\in\Sigma[x_{I_k}]\) implies \(p\ge0\) on \(K\).

notation.meaning: SOS polynomials in the clique-local polynomial ring.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and direct verification of a correlative-sparsity quadratic-module certificate; no existence claim is implicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A correlative-sparsity certificate is an identity \[p=\sum_{k=1}^s\left(\sigma_{0k}+\sum_{j\in J_k}\sigma_{jk}g_j\right),\qquad \sigma_{0k},\sigma_{jk}\in\Sigma[x_{I_k}],\] where every assigned constraint \(g_j\) uses only variables in \(I_k\). Each summand is nonnegative on \(K\), so the identity certifies \(p(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correlative-sparsity certificate is a sum of clique-local SOS quadratic-module identities using only variables and constraints assigned to each clique.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Local Quadratic-Module Certificate

assumptions_latex: The sets \(I_1,\ldots,I_s\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) satisfy the running-intersection property.
Every assigned constraint \(g_j\), \(j\in J_k\), belongs to \(\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\).
Each local module \(M_k=\Sigma[x_{I_k}]+\sum_{j\in J_k}\Sigma[x_{I_k}]g_j\) is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in M_1+\cdots+M_s\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by constraints assigned to clique \(I_k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse strict-positivity theorem; running intersection alone is not a completeness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the running-intersection property, clique-compatible constraint assignment, and local Archimedeanity, every strictly positive polynomial having a compatible decomposition \(f=\sum_k f_k\), \(f_k\in\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\), belongs to the sum of the local quadratic modules: \[f=\sum_{k=1}^s q_k,\qquad q_k\in M_k.\] Running intersection by itself does not imply this conclusion when the compatibility or local positivity hypotheses are absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under running intersection and local Archimedeanity, a strictly positive polynomial with a compatible clique decomposition has a sum of clique-local quadratic-module certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Putinar Positivstellensatz

assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x:g_j(x)ge0, j=1,ldots,m\}\) has variable cliques \(I_1,ldots,I_s\) satisfying the running-intersection property.
\(p=sum_{k=1}^s p_k\) with \(p_k\in\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\), and each constraint is assigned to a clique containing all its variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=sum_{k=1}^sleft(sigma_{0k}+sum_{jin J_k}sigma_{jk}g_jright)\) certifies \(pge0\) on \(K\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard sparse quadratic-module certificate under correlative sparsity and running intersection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-local sparse quadratic-module certificate; existence or convergence is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A correlative-sparsity certificate for \(p\) is an identity
\[
p=sum_{k=1}^sleft(sigma_{0k}+sum_{jin J_k}sigma_{jk}g_jright),
\]
where every \(sigma_{0k},sigma_{jk}\) is a sum of squares in \(mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\), and \(operatorname{var}(g_j)subseteq I_k\) whenever \(jin J_k\). Consequently each summand is nonnegative at every \(x\in K\), so \(p(x)ge0\) on \(K\). The running-intersection property organizes consistent overlaps between clique-local polynomial rings but is not itself sufficient to guarantee that every positive polynomial has such a certificate at a fixed degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polynomial is represented as a sum of clique-local SOS quadratic modules, using only variables and constraints assigned to each correlative-sparsity clique.
knowledge_statements.title: Correlative-Sparsity Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and clique-local formulation fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the precise role of the running-intersection and constraint-assignment assumptions. Extensive missing backslashes also corrupt the mathematical notation; a sourced formulation is required before repair.

assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) has degree at most \(2d\), and \(z\) is a fixed finite monomial vector.
\(\mathcal B=\{B_1,\ldots,B_t\}\) is a prescribed family of subsets of the indices of \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\sum_{\ell=1}^t z_{B_\ell}^{\mathsf T}Q_\ell z_{B_\ell}\), \(Q_\ell\succeq0\), certifies \(p\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Subvector of the fixed monomial vector indexed by block \(B_\ell\).
Cone of polynomials possessing a PSD block-Gram representation over \(\mathcal B\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-independent fixed-basis definition and expressiveness boundary; no particular support-extension algorithm is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A term-sparse SOS certificate in a fixed monomial basis \(z\) is a coefficient identity \[p(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^t z_{B_\ell}(x)^{\mathsf T}Q_\ell z_{B_\ell}(x),\qquad Q_\ell\succeq0.\] If every block in \(\mathcal B\) is contained in a block of \(\mathcal C\), then \(\operatorname{SOS}(\mathcal B)\subseteq\operatorname{SOS}(\mathcal C)\); one full block recovers the dense SOS cone on \(z\). For a proper restricted family this inclusion can be strict, so failure of the block certificate need not imply failure of dense SOS membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A term-sparse certificate uses PSD Gram blocks indexed by groups of monomials; merging blocks enlarges the cone, while restrictive blocks can miss dense SOS polynomials.
knowledge_statements.title: Term-Sparse Block-Gram Certificates

assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) has degree at most \(2d\), and \(z_d\) is a selected monomial vector.
\(mathcal B_1,ldots,mathcal B_t\) are monomial blocks obtained from a support graph compatible with the coefficient support of \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=sum_{ell=1}^t z_{mathcal B_ell}^{mathsf T}Q_ell z_{mathcal B_ell}\), \(Q_ellsucceq0\), is a verifiable sparse SOS certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard block-Gram formulation of term-sparse SOS certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-basis block-Gram definition; no completeness claim for a particular support-closure algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A term-sparsity certificate of degree \(2d\) is a coefficient identity
\[
p(x)=sum_{ell=1}^t z_{mathcal B_ell}(x)^{mathsf T}Q_ell z_{mathcal B_ell}(x),qquad Q_ellsucceq0,
\]
where the blocks \(mathcal B_ell\) are formed from monomials rather than variable cliques. Coefficient matching requires that every exponent produced by a block sum \(alpha+beta\), with \(alpha,betainmathcal B_ell\), is handled consistently with the chosen support graph and its closure. Positive semidefiniteness makes each block a sum of squares, hence the displayed identity certifies \(p(x)ge0\) for all \(x\inmathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A term-sparse certificate expresses the polynomial through positive-semidefinite Gram blocks indexed by connected groups of monomials in a support graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Term-Sparsity Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A block-Gram certificate indexed by monomials fits term sparsity, but the required compatibility and closure conditions depend on the particular support-graph construction and are not sourced. The displayed TeX is also corrupted.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^{|V|}_+\) and \(Q_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i\ne j\) and \(\{i,j\}\notin E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=\sum_{k=1}^s E_{C_k}^{\mathsf T}Q_kE_{C_k}\) for matrices \(Q_k\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Coordinate-selection matrix extracting entries indexed by clique \(C_k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse positive-semidefinite decomposition over maximal cliques of a chordal graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(G\) is chordal and the positive-semidefinite matrix \(Q\) has zeros outside the diagonal and edges of \(G\), then there are matrices \(Q_k\succeq0\), indexed by the maximal cliques, such that \[Q=\sum_{k=1}^s E_{C_k}^{\mathsf T}Q_kE_{C_k}.\] Consequently, a Gram identity \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\) becomes a sum of clique-local positive-semidefinite Gram identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordally sparse PSD Gram matrix is a sum of embedded PSD clique matrices, yielding clique-local polynomial certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Sparse-PSD Clique Decomposition

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a partial symmetric matrix specified on the diagonal and edges of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\) has a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if \(X[C]\succeq0\) for every maximal clique \(C\).

notation.meaning: Fully specified principal submatrix indexed by clique \(C\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion formulation and sharp chordality boundary for clique-wise PSD tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial symmetric matrix whose specified-entry graph \(G\) is chordal admits a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if every maximal-clique principal submatrix is positive semidefinite. For a nonchordal specified-entry graph, maximal-clique positive semidefiniteness alone is not sufficient in general; one may instead impose consistency through a chordal extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For chordal patterns, maximal-clique PSD tests exactly characterize PSD completability; this equivalence generally fails without chordality.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Positive-Semidefinite Completion Criterion

assumptions_latex: \(Qsucceq0\) is symmetric and has zeros outside the diagonal and edges of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=sum_{k=1}^s E_{C_k}^{mathsf T}Q_kE_{C_k}\) with \(Q_ksucceq0\), yielding a clique-wise polynomial certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard chordal decomposition of sparse positive-semidefinite matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal decomposition of a sparse Gram matrix over maximal cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a chordal graph \(G\), every positive-semidefinite matrix \(Q\) whose sparsity pattern is contained in \(G\) admits clique matrices \(Q_ksucceq0\) satisfying
\[
Q=sum_{k=1}^s E_{C_k}^{mathsf T}Q_kE_{C_k}.
\]
Thus, if \(p=z^{mathsf T}Qz\), then
\[
p=sum_{k=1}^s (E_{C_k}z)^{mathsf T}Q_k(E_{C_k}z),
\]
so global Gram-matrix positivity is certified through positive-semidefinite matrices supported on maximal cliques. For a nonchordal sparsity graph, the representation applies after choosing a chordal extension, whose added edges may enlarge the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordally sparse positive-semidefinite Gram matrix decomposes into embedded positive-semidefinite clique matrices, producing a sum of clique-local polynomial certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Certificate Decompositions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct kind for this leaf, and the claimed sparse-PSD clique decomposition is standard for chordal patterns. Nevertheless, no specific source is supplied for the theorem or selector convention, and the TeX contains pervasive command corruption.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^2\in\Sigma[x]^\Gamma\), but \(x^2\notin\{\sum_i h_i^2:h_i\in\mathbb R[x]^\Gamma\}\).

notation.meaning: Ring of polynomials invariant under the group action.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between an invariant SOS polynomial and a sum of squares of invariant polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the sign action \(x\mapsto-x\), the polynomial \(x^2\) is invariant and is a sum of squares. It cannot be written as \(\sum_i h_i(x)^2\) with every \(h_i\in\mathbb R[x^2]\), because nonconstant invariant squares have degree at least four and constant squares cannot produce the term \(x^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The invariant SOS polynomial x squared is not a sum of squares of invariant polynomials under the sign action.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invariant SOS Need Not Have Invariant Square Roots
knowledge_statements.title: Invariant SOS Need Not Have Invariant Square Roots

assumptions_latex: A finite group \(\Gamma\) acts linearly on \(\mathbb R^n\).
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) is a convex cone stable under the induced action of \(\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\mathcal R(p)\in C^\Gamma\), and averaging any certificate expression for \(p\) gives an invariant expression in \(C\).

notation.meaning: Invariant part of the certificate cone.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-group averaging of the complete expression in a group-stable convex certificate cone, including modules whose generators are permuted by the action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite group, the Reynolds operator \(\mathcal R(f)=|\Gamma|^{-1}\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}f\circ\gamma\) maps every convex, \(\Gamma\)-stable certificate cone \(C\) into \(C^\Gamma\). Hence an invariant polynomial \(p\in C\) has an invariant averaged certificate without changing \(p\). When constraints are permuted, invariance is asserted for the complete averaged module expression; individual multipliers or squared polynomials need not be invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-group-invariant certificate can be Reynolds-averaged inside any stable convex certificate cone, although its individual squares or multipliers need not be invariant.
knowledge_statements.title: Reynolds Symmetrization of Certificate Cones

assumptions_latex: A finite group \(Gamma\) acts linearly on \(mathbb R^n\), while \(p\) and the quadratic module \(M\) are \(Gamma\)-invariant.
\(pin M\) has a valid polynomial positivity certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Applying the Reynolds operator yields an invariant certificate \(p=mathcal R(c)\) with \(mathcal R(c)in M^Gamma\).

notation.meaning: Invariant part of the quadratic module

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-group averaging preserves invariant quadratic modules and SOS cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-group Reynolds averaging of an existing invariant quadratic-module certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the Reynolds operator by \(mathcal R(f)=|Gamma|^{-1}sum_{gammainGamma}fcircgamma\). If \(p\) is invariant and \(p=c\) is a certificate with \(cin M\), then
\[
p=mathcal R(p)=mathcal R(c).
\]
Because sums of squares are preserved by linear substitutions and convex averaging, and because \(M\) is stable under the group action, \(mathcal R(c)in M^Gamma\). Hence the averaged identity is an invariant-polynomial certificate of the same nonnegativity claim. Individual multipliers need not be invariant when the group permutes constraints; invariance is required of the complete averaged module expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-group-invariant positivity certificate can be averaged by the Reynolds operator to obtain an invariant certificate without changing the represented polynomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Polynomial Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A Reynolds-averaged certificate fits the invariant-polynomial leaf, but preservation of the complete quadratic module, especially when constraints are permuted, requires a specialized citation and precise hypotheses. The TeX commands are also corrupted.

assumptions_latex: \(\rho:\Gamma\to O(N)\) is a real orthogonal representation of a finite group.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An orthogonal isotypic basis makes \(Q\) block diagonal, and \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if every correctly typed reduced commutant block is positive semidefinite.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal representation on the Gram space.
Orthogonal change to a real isotypic basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real finite-group isotypic reduction stated at the commutant-algebra level, avoiding an invalid universal scalar-block convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An invariant symmetric Gram matrix lies in the self-adjoint part of the commutant of \(\rho(\Gamma)\). After an orthogonal decomposition into real isotypic components, \[U^{\mathsf T}QU=\bigoplus_{\lambda}Q_\lambda,\] with no coupling between inequivalent components. Each \(Q_\lambda\) acts through the multiplicity space over the real division algebra associated with the irreducible type, and \(Q\succeq0\) holds exactly when all these reduced blocks are positive semidefinite in their respective real, complex, or quaternionic Hermitian sense. Thus an invariant SOS Gram constraint reduces to independent smaller constraints. Treating every irreducible type as an ordinary real scalar multiplicity block is not valid in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invariant Gram matrix belongs to the representation commutant and reduces across real isotypic components to smaller PSD blocks, with real, complex, or quaternionic block types retained as required.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Isotypic Commutant Reduction of Invariant Gram Matrices
knowledge_statements.title: Isotypic Commutant Reduction of Invariant Gram Matrices

assumptions_latex: \(rho:Gammato O(N)\) is a finite-dimensional real orthogonal representation of a finite group.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An isotypic basis block-diagonalizes \(Q\), replacing one invariant PSD constraint by smaller multiplicity-space PSD constraints.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal group representation on the Gram space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: commutant decomposition of invariant PSD Gram matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real finite-group isotypic reduction; field-specific multiplicities require convention checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Decompose the Gram space orthogonally into real isotypic components for \(rho\). Since an invariant Gram matrix \(Q\) commutes with every \(rho(gamma)\), there is an orthogonal isotypic basis \(U\) in which
\[
U^{mathsf T}QU=bigoplus_{lambda} Q_lambda,
\]
with no coupling between inequivalent isotypic components and with each \(Q_lambda\) belonging to the corresponding commutant algebra. Moreover, \(Qsucceq0\) holds exactly when every reduced block is positive semidefinite in that algebra. Applied to an invariant SOS Gram representation, this replaces the full semidefinite constraint by independent representation-theoretic block constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetry-invariant Gram matrix lies in the representation commutant and becomes block diagonal across isotypic components, reducing the associated semidefinite constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Theoretic Block Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind matches the block-reduction leaf. A source is required to fix the real, complex, and quaternionic commutant conventions and to justify the exact reduced PSD constraints; the current TeX is additionally corrupted.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of the Diagonally Dominant Matrix Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-cone duality underlying fixed-basis DSOS optimization; coefficient-space duals also use the adjoint Gram map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cone \(\mathrm{DD}_N\) is generated by \(e_i e_i^{\mathsf T}\) and \((e_i\pm e_j)(e_i\pm e_j)^{\mathsf T}\) for \(i<j\). Hence \[\mathrm{DD}_N^*=\{X\in\mathbb S^N:X_{ii}\ge0,\ X_{ii}+X_{jj}\pm2X_{ij}\ge0\text{ for all }i<j\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual of the diagonally dominant matrix cone is determined by nonnegativity on coordinate vectors and signed two-coordinate vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm{DD}_N\) is the cone of symmetric diagonally dominant matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\mathrm{DD}_N^*\iff X_{ii}\ge0\) and \(X_{ii}+X_{jj}\pm2X_{ij}\ge0\) for every \(i<j\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone under the trace pairing

knowledge_statements.title: Dual of the Diagonally Dominant Matrix Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Basis DSOS Certificate and LP Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and membership formulation relative to a declared monomial vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed monomial vector \(z_d\), a polynomial \(p\) is DSOS relative to \(z_d\) if \[p=z_d^{\mathsf T}Qz_d,\qquad Q_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}|Q_{ij}|\quad(i=1,\ldots,N)\] for some symmetric \(Q\). Such \(Q\) is positive semidefinite, so the identity certifies \(p\ge0\). Coefficient matching together with variables \(u_{ij}\ge Q_{ij}\), \(u_{ij}\ge-Q_{ij}\), and \(Q_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}u_{ij}\) is a linear-programming feasibility formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DSOS polynomial has a diagonally dominant Gram matrix in a fixed monomial basis, and membership is an LP feasibility problem.
assumptions_latex: \(z_d\) is a fixed monomial vector spanning the selected Gram representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\in\mathrm{DSOS}(z_d)\Longrightarrow p(x)\ge0\text{ for every }x,\quad\mathrm{DSOS}(z_d)\text{ membership is LP-representable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Basis DSOS Certificate and LP Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Signed-Binomial Atomic Representation of DSOS Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent primal representation in the same fixed monomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=(m_1,\ldots,m_N)^{\mathsf T}\), \(Q\in\mathrm{DD}_N\) if and only if \[z^{\mathsf T}Qz=\sum_i a_im_i^2+\sum_{i<j}\left(b_{ij}^+(m_i+m_j)^2+b_{ij}^-(m_i-m_j)^2\right)\] for coefficients \(a_i,b_{ij}^+,b_{ij}^-\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DSOS forms are exactly nonnegative sums of monomial squares and squares of signed pairs of basis monomials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\in\mathrm{DD}_N\iff z^{\mathsf T}Qz\text{ has the displayed signed-binomial-square representation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Signed-Binomial Atomic Representation of DSOS Forms

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A diagonally dominant Gram matrix \(Q\) satisfying \(p=z_d^{mathsf T}Qz_d\) is a DSOS certificate of global nonnegativity.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard fixed-basis definition of a DSOS polynomial
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-monomial-basis DSOS certificate represented by linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The polynomial \(p\) is diagonally-dominant-sum-of-squares, or DSOS, relative to \(z_d\), if there exists a symmetric matrix \(Q\) such that
\[
p(x)=z_d(x)^{mathsf T}Qz_d(x),qquad Q_{ii}gesum_{jne i}|Q_{ij}|quadtext{for every }i.
\]
Diagonal dominance with nonnegative diagonal implies \(Qsucceq0\), so the identity certifies \(p(x)ge0\) on \(mathbb R^n\). Introducing variables \(u_{ij}gepm Q_{ij}\) converts diagonal dominance and coefficient matching into linear constraints, making membership in this fixed-basis certificate cone testable by linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DSOS certificate is an SOS Gram representation whose fixed-basis Gram matrix is diagonally dominant, so membership can be tested by linear programming.
knowledge_statements.title: DSOS Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-basis diagonally dominant Gram certificate is appropriate for this leaf, but neither the DSOS definition nor its LP formulation has an inspectable citation. Numerous missing backslashes make the formulas invalid.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-cone duality; coefficient-space duals also require the adjoint polynomial Gram map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N\ge2\), \(X\in\mathrm{SDD}_N^*\) exactly when every two-by-two principal submatrix \(\begin{pmatrix}X_{ii}&X_{ij}\\X_{ij}&X_{jj}\end{pmatrix}\) is positive semidefinite, equivalently when \(X_{ii}\ge0\) and \(X_{ij}^2\le X_{ii}X_{jj}\) for all \(i<j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual of the scaled diagonally dominant cone consists of matrices whose two-by-two principal submatrices are positive semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm{SDD}_N\) is the sum of positive-semidefinite cones embedded on principal index sets of size at most two.
The pairing is the trace inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\mathrm{SDD}_N^*\iff X[\{i,j\}]\succeq0\) for every \(i<j\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Basis SDSOS Certificate and SOCP Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition, equivalent two-block representation, and conic membership test in a fixed monomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed monomial vector \(z_d\), a polynomial \(p\) is SDSOS relative to \(z_d\) if \(p=z_d^{\mathsf T}Qz_d\) for a symmetric matrix \(Q\) such that \(DQD\) is diagonally dominant for some positive diagonal \(D\). Equivalently, \[Q=\sum_{i<j}E_{ij}^{\mathsf T}Q^{ij}E_{ij},\qquad Q^{ij}\in\mathbb S_+^2,\] allowing degenerate blocks for diagonal terms. Each condition \(Q^{ij}\succeq0\) is representable by a rotated second-order cone. Hence fixed-basis SDSOS membership is an SOCP feasibility problem, and \(Q\succeq0\) certifies \(p\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDSOS certificate uses a scaled diagonally dominant Gram matrix, equivalently a sum of embedded two-by-two PSD blocks, so membership is SOCP-representable.
assumptions_latex: The Gram dimension is at least two; one-dimensional cases reduce to a nonnegative scalar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\in\mathrm{SDSOS}(z_d)\Longrightarrow p(x)\ge0\text{ for every }x,\quad\mathrm{SDSOS}(z_d)\text{ membership is SOCP-representable}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-monomial-basis SDSOS certificate represented by second-order-cone constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The polynomial \(p\) is scaled-diagonally-dominant-sum-of-squares, or SDSOS, relative to \(z_d\), if
\[
p(x)=z_d(x)^{mathsf T}Qz_d(x)
\]
for a symmetric matrix \(Q\) for which some positive diagonal \(D\) makes \(DQD\) diagonally dominant. Equivalently, \(Q\) is a sum of positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices, each supported on a principal block of size at most two. This characterization gives second-order-cone constraints, implies \(Qsucceq0\), and therefore makes the displayed identity a certificate that \(p(x)ge0\) for every \(xinmathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDSOS certificate uses a Gram matrix made diagonally dominant by positive diagonal scaling; its two-by-two block characterization permits SOCP testing.
knowledge_statements.title: SDSOS Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and fixed-basis SDSOS formulation fit the leaf. The equivalence between positive diagonal scaling, two-by-two PSD decomposition, and SOCP representability needs a specialized source, and the TeX is corrupted.

children.title: Relative Cone Expressiveness
children.top_down_role: Expressiveness relationships among DSOS, SDSOS, plus broader sum-of-squares cones.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed homogeneous bases with unique quadratic Gram matrices; no strictness claim is made for every basis or dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=(x_1,x_2)^{\mathsf T}\), \((x_1+2x_2)^2\) has Gram matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}\), which is scaled diagonally dominant but not diagonally dominant. For \(z=(x_1,x_2,x_3)^{\mathsf T}\), \((x_1+x_2+x_3)^2\) has Gram matrix \(J_3\), which is positive semidefinite but not scaled diagonally dominant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared binomial separates SDSOS from DSOS, and the square of a three-term sum separates SOS from SDSOS in fixed homogeneous bases.
assumptions_latex: Homogeneous quadratic forms use the degree-one monomial vector, so their symmetric Gram matrix is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed examples establish strict fixed-basis inclusions \(\mathrm{DSOS}\subsetneq\mathrm{SDSOS}\subsetneq\mathrm{SOS}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Fixed-Basis Cone Separations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone comparison at one fixed degree and monomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed monomial vector \(z_d\), \[\mathrm{DSOS}(z_d)\subseteq\mathrm{SDSOS}(z_d)\subseteq\mathrm{SOS}(z_d).\] The first inclusion follows from \(\mathrm{DD}_N\subseteq\mathrm{SDD}_N\), and the second from \(\mathrm{SDD}_N\subseteq\mathbb S_+^N\). These comparisons require the same Gram basis. Permutations preserve both restricted matrix cones; positive diagonal congruences preserve \(\mathrm{SDD}_N\) but need not preserve \(\mathrm{DD}_N\), and general nonsingular congruences need preserve neither.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a common basis, DSOS is contained in SDSOS, which is contained in SOS; restricted Gram membership is basis-sensitive.
assumptions_latex: One degree bound and monomial vector \(z_d\) are used for all three cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{DSOS}(z_d)\subseteq\mathrm{SDSOS}(z_d)\subseteq\mathrm{SOS}(z_d).
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Basis DSOS–SDSOS–SOS Inclusion Chain

assumptions_latex: A degree bound and monomial vector \(z_d\) are fixed for all three Gram cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(mathrm{DSOS}(z_d)subseteqmathrm{SDSOS}(z_d)subseteqmathrm{SOS}(z_d)\).

notation.meaning: DSOS cone in the selected basis
SDSOS cone in the selected basis
SOS Gram cone in the selected basis

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: diagonal dominance implies scaled diagonal dominance, which implies positive semidefiniteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone inclusions for one fixed degree and monomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed monomial vector \(z_d\), every diagonally dominant Gram matrix is scaled diagonally dominant by taking the identity scaling, and every scaled diagonally dominant matrix is positive semidefinite. Consequently,
\[
mathrm{DSOS}(z_d)subseteqmathrm{SDSOS}(z_d)subseteqmathrm{SOS}(z_d).
\]
The inclusions compare certificates using the same basis and degree bound; DSOS and SDSOS membership may change under a general basis transformation. The reverse inclusions fail in general because the cones of diagonally dominant and scaled diagonally dominant matrices are proper inner approximations of the positive-semidefinite cone once the Gram dimension is sufficiently large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a fixed monomial basis, DSOS certificates are contained in SDSOS certificates, which are contained in SOS certificates; the reverse inclusions generally fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Cone Expressiveness

children.title: Tractability Gaps
children.top_down_role: Positivity instances excluded by these restricted inner certificate cones.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic formulation size at fixed Gram dimension; not a solver-independent runtime bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Gram dimension \(N\), diagonal dominance uses \(O(N^2)\) linear inequalities after introducing off-diagonal absolute-value variables. Scaled diagonal dominance uses \(O(N^2)\) embedded two-by-two PSD, equivalently rotated-second-order-cone, blocks. Unrestricted SOS Gram feasibility uses one \(N\times N\) positive-semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DSOS uses quadratically many linear inequalities, SDSOS uses quadratically many small conic blocks, and SOS uses one full PSD constraint.
assumptions_latex: A monomial vector of length \(N\) and the coefficient-matching equations are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{DD}_N\text{ is LP-representable},\quad\mathrm{SDD}_N\text{ is SOCP-representable},\quad\mathbb S_+^N\text{ requires a full PSD constraint}.

notation.meaning: DD, SDD, and PSD matrix cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Dimension Constraint Architecture

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative bound comparison at a common basis, degree, and optimization formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(\mathbb S_+^N\) by \(\mathrm{SDD}_N\) or \(\mathrm{DD}_N\) yields cheaper conic formulations but restricts the available Gram certificates. At a common basis and degree, \[\mathrm{DD}_N\subseteq\mathrm{SDD}_N\subseteq\mathbb S_+^N,\] so for a maximized polynomial lower bound the corresponding optimal values satisfy \[\gamma_{\mathrm{DSOS}}\le\gamma_{\mathrm{SDSOS}}\le\gamma_{\mathrm{SOS}}.\] Because the polynomial certificate cones are strictly separated in suitable fixed bases, either inequality can be strict for suitable coefficient-matching optimization data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LP and SOCP Gram restrictions can be cheaper than SDP but can lose certificates and yield strictly weaker fixed-degree lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: All relaxations use the same polynomial basis, degree bound, coefficient equations, and lower-bound objective.
The optimization problem maximizes a certified scalar lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma_{\mathrm{DSOS}}\le\gamma_{\mathrm{SDSOS}}\le\gamma_{\mathrm{SOS}},\text{ with strict inequalities possible}.

notation.meaning: Optimal certified lower bounds from the three common-order formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Degree Tractability–Expressiveness Gap

assumptions_latex: The monomial basis and relaxation degree are fixed, and Gram-matrix dimension is \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: DSOS uses LP, SDSOS uses SOCP, and SOS uses SDP, while the cheaper cones can yield strictly weaker bounds.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard conic formulations and strict inner-cone limitation of DSOS and SDSOS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative tractability-expressiveness boundary at a fixed relaxation degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Coefficient matching plus diagonal dominance gives an \(mathrm{LP}\) formulation for DSOS; scaled diagonal dominance gives an \(mathrm{SOCP}\) formulation for SDSOS; unrestricted Gram positivity gives an \(mathrm{SDP}\) formulation for SOS. Thus the first two avoid a full \(Ntimes N\) semidefinite constraint. The tractability gain has a certificate gap: because
\[
mathrm{DD}_Nsubseteqmathrm{SDD}_Nsubseteqmathbb S_+^N
\]
are generally proper inclusions, an SOS polynomial may lack an SDSOS, and hence a DSOS, Gram certificate in the selected basis. Corresponding optimization lower bounds can therefore be strictly weaker at the same degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DSOS and SDSOS replace semidefinite constraints by LP and SOCP constraints, respectively, but may lose certificates and produce weaker fixed-degree optimization bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Tractability Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary appropriately captures the tractability–expressiveness gap. A specialized source is needed for the LP, SOCP, and SDP formulations and for the strict fixed-degree bound gap; the current formulas are syntactically corrupted.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate circuit supports are fixed; support selection and sufficiency of the chosen family are outside this subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For prescribed circuits with \(\beta_k=\sum_i\lambda_{k,i}\alpha_{k,i}\), introduce \(c_{k,i}\ge0\) and inner coefficients \(d_k\), impose linear coefficient matching, and impose \(|d_k|\le\prod_i(c_{k,i}/\lambda_{k,i})^{\lambda_{k,i}}\) when \(\beta_k\notin(2\mathbb N)^n\), or \(d_k\ge-\prod_i(c_{k,i}/\lambda_{k,i})^{\lambda_{k,i}}\) when \(\beta_k\in(2\mathbb N)^n\). These weighted-geometric-mean constraints admit convex power-cone formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed candidate circuits, coefficient matching and circuit-number inequalities form a convex power-cone feasibility problem yielding an explicit SONC decomposition.
assumptions_latex: A finite family of circuit supports is prescribed.
Each inner exponent has fixed positive barycentric weights relative to its outer simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility of coefficient matching and the circuit-number inequalities produces a SONC decomposition.

notation.meaning: Outer coefficient allocated to circuit k

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Circuit SONC Conic Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parity-dependent global nonnegativity criterion and finite-sum SONC definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[f(x)=\sum_{i=0}^r c_i x^{\alpha_i}+c_\beta x^\beta,\] where \(c_i>0\), the \(\alpha_i\in(2\mathbb N)^n\) are affinely independent, and \(\beta=\sum_i\lambda_i\alpha_i\) with \(\lambda_i>0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\). Define \[\Theta_f=\prod_{i=0}^r\left(\frac{c_i}{\lambda_i}\right)^{\lambda_i}.\] Then \(f\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(|c_\beta|\le\Theta_f\) when \(\beta\notin(2\mathbb N)^n\), and if and only if \(c_\beta\ge-\Theta_f\) when \(\beta\in(2\mathbb N)^n\). The SONC cone consists of finite sums of circuit polynomials satisfying these conditions, including nonnegative monomial squares as degenerate summands.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A circuit polynomial is nonnegative exactly at its parity-dependent circuit-number threshold, and SONC polynomials are finite sums of such circuits.
assumptions_latex: Outer exponents are even and affinely independent.
The inner exponent lies in their relative interior with positive barycentric weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\ge0\iff\begin{cases}|c_\beta|\le\Theta_f,&\beta\notin(2\mathbb N)^n,\\c_\beta\ge-\Theta_f,&\beta\in(2\mathbb N)^n.\end{cases}

notation.meaning: Barycentric coordinates of the inner exponent.

knowledge_statements.title: Circuit-Number Criterion and SONC Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Power-Cone Conditions for Fixed Circuits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuitwise duality; a full coefficient-space dual also includes the adjoint coefficient-matching equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive weights \(\lambda_i\) summing to one, define \[C_\lambda=\left\{(c,d):c_i\ge0,\ |d|\le\prod_i\left(\frac{c_i}{\lambda_i}\right)^{\lambda_i}\right\}.\] Under the Euclidean pairing, \[C_\lambda^*=\left\{(u,w):u_i\ge0,\ |w|\le\prod_i u_i^{\lambda_i}\right\}.\] For the even-inner one-sided cone \(d\ge-\prod_i(c_i/\lambda_i)^{\lambda_i}\), the dual conditions are \(u_i\ge0\), \(w\ge0\), and \(w\le\prod_i u_i^{\lambda_i}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed circuit has an explicit weighted-geometric-mean dual cone, with a nonnegative inner dual coordinate in the even-inner one-sided case.
assumptions_latex: The standard Euclidean pairing is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_\lambda^*=\{(u,w):u_i\ge0,\ |w|\le\prod_i u_i^{\lambda_i}\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Power-Cone Conditions for Fixed Circuits

assumptions_latex: Each circuit polynomial has even affinely independent outer exponents and one exponent in their relative interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sum of circuit polynomials satisfying the circuit-number inequalities is a SONC certificate of global nonnegativity.

notation.meaning: Barycentric coordinates of the inner exponent

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard nonnegative circuit-polynomial criterion and SONC cone definition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global SONC certificate using the standard circuit-number nonnegativity criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=sum_{i=0}^r c_i x^{alpha_i}+c_beta x^beta\), where \(c_i>0\), the \(alpha_iin(2mathbb N)^n\) are affinely independent, and \(beta=sum_ilambda_ialpha_i\) with \(lambda_i>0\) and \(sum_ilambda_i=1\). Define
\[
Theta_f=prod_{i=0}^rleft(frac{c_i}{lambda_i}right)^{lambda_i}.
\]
Then \(f\) is nonnegative exactly when \(|c_beta|leTheta_f\) if \(betanotin(2mathbb N)^n\), and when \(c_betage-Theta_f\) if \(betain(2mathbb N)^n\). An identity expressing \(p\) as a finite sum of such nonnegative circuit polynomials is a SONC certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A SONC certificate decomposes a polynomial into circuit polynomials whose inner coefficients satisfy explicit circuit-number inequalities ensuring global nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.title: SONC Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The circuit-number criterion and finite-sum certificate fit the SONC leaf, but the exact even and noneven inner-exponent cases require a specialized citation. The mathematical TeX is extensively malformed.

children.title: Diagonal-Tail Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates for forms organized around diagonal terms plus a restricted tail.

assumptions_latex: \(f=\sum_{i=1}^N b_i x^{\alpha_i}+\sum_{\beta\in T}c_\beta x^\beta\), where \(b_i\ge0\) and \(\alpha_i\in(2\mathbb N)^n\).

For each \(\beta\in T\), an affinely independent set \(V_\beta\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\) is chosen such that \(\beta=\sum_{i\in V_\beta}\lambda_{i\beta}\alpha_i\), with \(\lambda_{i\beta}>0\) and \(\sum_{i\in V_\beta}\lambda_{i\beta}=1\).
Allocations satisfy \(a_{i\beta}>0\) for \(i\in V_\beta\), \(a_{i\beta}=0\) otherwise, and \(\sum_{\beta\in T}a_{i\beta}\le b_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated circuit-number bounds imply \(f(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Circuit number of the component allocated to tail \(\beta\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient allocation certificate with positive allocations only on the active affinely independent support of each tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every tail \(\beta\), define \[\Theta_\beta=\prod_{i\in V_\beta}\left(\frac{a_{i\beta}}{\lambda_{i\beta}}\right)^{\lambda_{i\beta}}.\] Require \(|c_\beta|\le\Theta_\beta\) when \(\beta\notin(2\mathbb N)^n\), and require \(c_\beta\ge-\Theta_\beta\) when \(\beta\in(2\mathbb N)^n\). Then each polynomial \(\sum_{i\in V_\beta}a_{i\beta}x^{\alpha_i}+c_\beta x^\beta\) is nonnegative, and every residual term \((b_i-\sum_\beta a_{i\beta})x^{\alpha_i}\) is a nonnegative monomial square. Their sum certifies \(f\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Failure to find such allocations does not by itself imply that \(f\) is negative or lacks a certificate in a broader cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate diagonal coefficients to each tail so every resulting circuit satisfies its circuit-number bound; unused diagonal coefficients remain nonnegative monomial squares.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Tail Allocation Certificate

assumptions_latex: \(f=sum_{i=0}^r b_i x^{2alpha_i}+sum_{betain T}c_beta x^beta\), where \(b_i>0\) and every tail exponent lies in \(operatorname{conv}{2alpha_0,ldots,2alpha_r}\).
For each \(beta\), choose barycentric weights \(lambda_{ibeta}\) and allocations \(a_{ibeta}ge0\) with \(sum_beta a_{ibeta}le b_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The allocation and circuit-number inequalities decompose \(f\) into nonnegative diagonal-tail circuits and nonnegative monomial squares.

notation.meaning: Diagonal coefficient allocated to tail beta

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: diagonal-minus-tail allocation into nonnegative circuit polynomials via weighted AM-GM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient allocation certificate for diagonal-plus-tail polynomials with interior tail exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write each \(beta\in T\) as \(beta=sum_ilambda_{ibeta}(2alpha_i)\), using only positive weights on its minimal containing face, and define
\[
Theta_beta=prod_{i:lambda_{ibeta}>0}left(frac{a_{ibeta}}{lambda_{ibeta}}right)^{lambda_{ibeta}}.
\]
Require \(|c_beta|leTheta_beta\) for a noneven tail exponent and \(c_betage-Theta_beta\) for an even tail exponent. Then each allocated polynomial \(sum_i a_{ibeta}x^{2alpha_i}+c_beta x^beta\) is nonnegative. Since every residual coefficient \(b_i-sum_beta a_{ibeta}\) is nonnegative, their sum gives a verifiable certificate that \(fge0\) on \(mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal coefficients are allocated among tail monomials so each resulting circuit satisfies its circuit-number bound; unused diagonal terms remain nonnegative monomial squares.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Tail Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the diagonal-tail leaf, but the stated assumptions do not ensure that the selected outer exponents form the affine-independent circuit support needed for every tail. Allowing zero allocations on positive barycentric coordinates also requires explicit boundary conventions. These issues and the corrupted TeX cannot be resolved without a specialized source.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted affine dependence defines an agiform whose even outer monomials dominate the absolute value of the inner monomial, so the resulting polynomial is globally nonnegative.

children.title: Support-Geometry Relations
children.top_down_role: Shared exponent-support structures connecting diagonal-tail forms to agiforms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine support geometry only; no positivity-certificate conclusion is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_r\}\) be affinely independent and let \(F\) be the minimal face of \(\operatorname{conv}V\) containing \(\beta\in\operatorname{conv}V\). In the unique representation \(\beta=\sum_{i=0}^r\lambda_i\alpha_i\), \(\lambda_i\ge0\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), one has \(\lambda_i>0\) exactly for the vertices of \(F\), and \(\lambda_i=0\) outside \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive barycentric weights of a simplex point identify exactly the vertices of its minimal face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_i>0\) exactly on the vertices of the minimal face containing \(\beta\).

notation.meaning: Minimal face containing the designated exponent

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Face Reduction of Barycentric Support

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Interior and Positive Barycentric Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational simplex-support geometry used by agiform and circuit certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_r\}\subset\mathbb R^n\) be affinely independent. Every \(\beta\in\operatorname{aff}V\) has unique coefficients \(\lambda_i\) satisfying \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\) and \(\beta=\sum_i\lambda_i\alpha_i\). Moreover, \[\beta\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}V)\iff \lambda_i>0\quad\text{for all }i.\] For circuit and agiform supports, these unique positive coordinates are precisely the weighted-AM-GM weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exponent is inside an outer simplex exactly when its unique barycentric coordinates are all positive; those coordinates are the circuit or agiform weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}V)\iff\lambda_i>0\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: Unique barycentric coordinates of the designated exponent.

assumptions_latex: \(\beta\in\mathbb N^n\) lies in the relative interior of \(\operatorname{conv}V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are unique \(\lambda_i>0\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\) and \(\beta=\sum_i\lambda_i\alpha_i\), and these weights determine the agiform inequality.

notation.meaning: Barycentric coordinates of the inner exponent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: This records the simplex-support geometry underlying one-tail agiform and circuit certificates.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.1 Elementary algebraic geometry p. 35

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Affine independence of \(V\) makes every point of \(\operatorname{aff}V\) have unique barycentric coordinates. The condition \(\beta\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}V)\) is equivalent to the existence of unique coefficients \(\lambda_i>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=0}^r\lambda_i=1\) and \(\beta=\sum_{i=0}^r\lambda_i\alpha_i\). These coefficients are exactly the weights in the associated weighted arithmetic-geometric mean certificate and determine its coefficient threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner exponent lies strictly inside the outer support simplex exactly when it has unique positive barycentric weights, which become the agiform weights.

children.title: Representability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Support configurations lying beyond these specialized certificate families.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary Support Requiring More Than One Circuit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates failure of the full-support single-circuit form from SONC representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polynomial \[p(x,y)=1+x^4+y^4-2x^2\] has outer simplex \(V=\{(0,0),(4,0),(0,4)\}\) and tail exponent \(\beta=(2,0)\) on a proper face of \(\operatorname{conv}V\), so its full support is not one circuit. Nevertheless, \[p=(1+x^4-2x^2)+y^4=(x^2-1)^2+y^4\] is a sum of a face-supported nonnegative circuit polynomial and a monomial square.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tail on a simplex face can prevent one full-support circuit while still allowing a sum of circuit and monomial-square certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\text{ is not one circuit on }V\cup\{\beta\}\text{ but is SONC}.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Support Requiring More Than One Circuit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes support eligibility for one simplex-supported agiform or circuit, not for sums of certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_r\}\subset(2\mathbb N)^n\) be affinely independent, and suppose every outer coefficient on \(V\) is positive. A polynomial with exact support \(V\cup\{\beta\}\) can have this entire support as one circuit only if \(\beta\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}V)\). If \(\beta\) lies on a proper face, the positive barycentric coordinates select a smaller circuit on that face, while outer monomials off the face must be handled separately. If \(\beta\notin\operatorname{conv}V\), no such circuit reduction exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One circuit requires its tail exponent inside the outer simplex; a boundary tail reduces to its minimal face, and an exterior tail is ineligible.
assumptions_latex: All monomials indexed by \(V\) have positive coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full support \(V\cup\{\beta\}\) is a single circuit only when \(\beta\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}V)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Circuit Support Boundary

assumptions_latex: A polynomial has support \(V\cup\{\beta\}\) with exactly one designated tail exponent \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single agiform certificate of this support type requires \(\beta\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}V)\); otherwise this certificate form is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The boundary concerns representation by one simplex-supported agiform, not sums of certificates.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.1 Elementary algebraic geometry p. 35

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A one-tail agiform supported on \(V\cup\{\beta\}\) requires positive weights \(\lambda_i\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\) and \(\beta=\sum_i\lambda_i\alpha_i\). Hence \(\beta\notin\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}V)\) prevents representation by this single certificate form. Likewise, affinely dependent outer support falls outside the simplex-supported form unless a suitable affinely independent subsupport is selected. These obstructions do not exclude representation as a sum of agiform or other positivity certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single simplex-supported agiform needs its tail exponent strictly inside the outer simplex; boundary, exterior, or nonsimplicial support requires reduction or multiple certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Representability Boundaries
