knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For variables \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), the truncated sum-of-squares cone at order \(d\) is \[\Sigma[x]_{2d}:=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^N q_j(x)^2:N\in\mathbb N,\ q_j\in\mathbb R[x],\ \deg q_j\le d\right\}.\] Every member has degree at most \(2d\) and is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^n\). The set is a convex cone, and membership is representable by a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix indexed by monomials of degree at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-d truncated SOS cone consists of sums of squares of polynomials of degree at most d and admits a positive-semidefinite Gram representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated SOS Cones

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Quadratic Modules and Preorderings p. 60

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}\iff\exists Q\succeq0:\ p=z_d^TQz_d\), where \(Q\) has order \(\binom{n+d}{d}\).

notation.meaning: Vector of all monomials of total degree at most d.
Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices of order s.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional membership in the unconstrained truncated SOS cone, rather than membership in a constrained module or preordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=\binom{n+d}{d}\). Membership of \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}\) in \(\Sigma[x]_{2d}\) is equivalent to feasibility of \[Q\in\mathbb S_+^s,\qquad p(x)=z_d(x)^TQz_d(x).\] Coefficient matching gives \(\binom{n+2d}{2d}\) scalar linear equations in the \(s(s+1)/2\) independent entries of \(Q\). Every feasible \(Q\) is a Gram certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated SOS membership is an SDP feasibility problem with a positive-semidefinite matrix indexed by degree-d monomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semidefinite Membership Test and Gram Size
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Membership Test and Gram Size

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), but \(M\notin\Sigma[x,y]_6\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic failure boundary of the unconstrained SOS cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Motzkin polynomial \[M(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4+1-3x^2y^2\] is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^2\) but is not a sum of squares. Thus \(M\in\mathbb R[x,y]_{\le6}\) while \(M\notin\Sigma[x,y]_6\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The degree-six Motzkin polynomial is globally nonnegative but does not belong to the degree-six SOS cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonnegativity Is Strictly Weaker Than SOS Membership
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegativity Is Strictly Weaker Than SOS Membership

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma[x]_{2d}\) is closed, pointed, and full-dimensional, with \(\operatorname{int}\Sigma[x]_{2d}=\{z_d^TQz_d:Q\succ0\}\).

notation.meaning: Vector of all monomials of total degree at most d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex geometry intrinsic to the truncated SOS cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cone \(\Sigma[x]_{2d}\subseteq\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}\) is closed, convex, pointed, and full-dimensional. Its interior is \[\operatorname{int}\Sigma[x]_{2d}=\{z_d(x)^TQz_d(x):Q\succ0\}.\] Hence a polynomial is interior exactly when it admits a positive-definite Gram representation on the full degree-\(d\) monomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The truncated SOS cone is closed, pointed, and full-dimensional, and its interior consists of polynomials admitting a positive-definite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Geometry and Interior

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma[x]_{2d}=\Sigma[x]_{2e}\cap\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact nesting with the ambient-degree intersection made explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(e\ge d\), \[\Sigma[x]_{2d}\subseteq\Sigma[x]_{2e},\qquad \Sigma[x]_{2d}=\Sigma[x]_{2e}\cap\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}.\] Thus higher-degree squared summands cannot produce a new SOS polynomial whose resulting degree remains at most \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated SOS cones are nested, and intersection with the lower-degree ambient space recovers the lower-order cone exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Nesting of Truncated SOS Cones
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Nesting of Truncated SOS Cones

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d(g)=\{\sum_{i=0}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\}\).

notation.meaning: Order-d truncated quadratic module generated by the constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The total degree of each weighted generator is bounded by \(2d\).

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Quadratic Modules and Preorderings p. 60

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The order-\(d\) truncated quadratic module generated by \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) is \[M_d(g):=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\text{ for }i=0,\ldots,m\right\},\] where \(g_0=1\). If \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), then every element of \(M_d(g)\) is nonnegative on \(K\), and \(M_d(g)\subseteq M_{d+1}(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated quadratic module contains SOS-weighted individual generators whose products have degree at most twice the relaxation order; every member is nonnegative on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Quadratic Modules

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Quadratic Modules and Preorderings p. 60

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone characterization for the finite total-degree truncation; it does not imply existence of a representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_y\) act on \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}\). Then
\[
L_y\in M_d(g)^*\iff M_d(y)\succeq0\quad\text{and}\quad M_{r_i}(g_iy)\succeq0
\]
for every \(i\ge1\) with \(\deg g_i\le2d\), where \(r_i=\lfloor(2d-\deg g_i)/2\rfloor\) and \(q^{\mathsf T}M_{r_i}(g_iy)q=L_y(g_iq^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual truncated-module cone consists exactly of functionals with a PSD moment matrix and PSD localizing matrices for every active generator.
assumptions_latex: \(L_y\) is a linear functional on \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}\).
The same per-term total-degree truncation as in \(M_d(g)\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_y\in M_d(g)^*\iff M_d(y)\succeq0\text{ and }M_{r_i}(g_iy)\succeq0\text{ for every active }i.

notation.meaning: Linear functional represented by truncated data y.
Moment matrix associated with the unit generator.
Dual cone of the truncated quadratic module.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Moment-Localizing Characterization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense finite-dimensional SDP representation under the seed's per-term total-degree convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_0=1\), \(\delta_i=\deg g_i\), and \(r_i=\lfloor(2d-\delta_i)/2\rfloor\) for every \(i\) with \(\delta_i\le2d\). Then
\[
f\in M_d(g)\iff f=\sum_{i:\delta_i\le2d}g_iv_{r_i}^{\mathsf T}Q_iv_{r_i},\qquad Q_i\succeq0.
\]
Exact coefficient matching therefore characterizes membership using at most \(m+1\) PSD blocks, with active block \(i\) of order \(\binom{n+r_i}{r_i}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated quadratic module has one degree-compatible PSD Gram block for the unit and each active individual generator, with exact coefficient matching characterizing membership.
assumptions_latex: Each \(v_{r_i}\) is the full total-degree monomial vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in M_d(g)\iff f=\sum_{i:\delta_i\le2d}g_iv_{r_i}^{\mathsf T}Q_iv_{r_i},\quad Q_i\succeq0.

notation.meaning: Maximum degree of square factors in the i-th multiplier.
PSD Gram matrix for the i-th SOS multiplier.

knowledge_statements.title: Generator-Indexed Gram Representation

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_d(g)=\{\sum_{I\subseteq[m]}\sigma_I g_I:\sigma_I\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_Ig_I)\le2d\}\).

notation.meaning: Squarefree product of generators indexed by a subset.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The preordering uses all squarefree products of the inequality generators.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Quadratic Modules and Preorderings p. 60

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), set \(g_I=\prod_{i\in I}g_i\), with \(g_\varnothing=1\). The order-\(d\) truncated preordering is \[T_d(g):=\left\{\sum_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}}\sigma_Ig_I:\sigma_I\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_Ig_I)\le2d\right\}.\] Every member is nonnegative on \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\}\), and \(M_d(g)\subseteq T_d(g)\), subject to the same total-degree convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated preordering allows SOS multiples of every squarefree product of constraints, with each term bounded by the chosen certificate degree.
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Preorderings

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Quadratic Modules and Preorderings p. 60

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone characterization for the finite total-degree truncation; it does not imply existence of a representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_y\) act on \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}\). Then
\[
L_y\in T_d(g)^*\iff M_{r_I}(g_Iy)\succeq0
\]
for every \(I\subseteq[m]\) with \(\deg g_I\le2d\), where \(r_I=\lfloor(2d-\deg g_I)/2\rfloor\) and \(q^{\mathsf T}M_{r_I}(g_Iy)q=L_y(g_Iq^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual truncated-preordering cone consists exactly of functionals whose localizing matrix is PSD for every active squarefree product.
assumptions_latex: \(L_y\) is a linear functional on \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}\).
The same per-term total-degree truncation as in \(T_d(g)\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_y\in T_d(g)^*\iff M_{r_I}(g_Iy)\succeq0\text{ for every active }I.

notation.meaning: Linear functional represented by truncated data y.
Localizing matrix for the squarefree product g_I.
Dual cone of the truncated preordering.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense finite-dimensional SDP representation under the seed's per-term total-degree convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(I\subseteq[m]\) with \(\delta_I:=\deg g_I\le2d\), set \(r_I=\lfloor(2d-\delta_I)/2\rfloor\). Then
\[
f\in T_d(g)\iff f=\sum_{I:\delta_I\le2d}g_Iv_{r_I}^{\mathsf T}Q_Iv_{r_I},\qquad Q_I\succeq0.
\]
Thus exact coefficient matching and one PSD block of order \(\binom{n+r_I}{r_I}\) for each active product characterize membership. Products of degree greater than \(2d\) are inactive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated preordering has one degree-compatible PSD Gram block for every active squarefree constraint product, with exact coefficient matching characterizing membership.
assumptions_latex: \(g_I=\prod_{i\in I}g_i\), and truncation is imposed separately by \(\deg(\sigma_Ig_I)\le2d\).
Each \(v_{r_I}\) is the full total-degree monomial vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in T_d(g)\iff f=\sum_{I:\delta_I\le2d}g_Iv_{r_I}^{\mathsf T}Q_Iv_{r_I},\quad Q_I\succeq0.

notation.meaning: Degree of the squarefree generator product.
Maximum degree of square factors in the corresponding multiplier.
PSD Gram matrix for the product's SOS multiplier.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a finite order \(d\) such that \(f\in T_d(g)\); an effective Schmüdgen bound supplies an explicit upper bound for the least such \(d\).

notation.meaning: Minimum positivity margin on the feasible set.
Least truncated-preordering order certifying the polynomial.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: This states the effective-bound interface; the numerical rate depends on normalization and geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Schmüdgen positivity implies \(d_{\mathrm{Sch}}(f;g)<\infty\). An effective version specifies a computable function \(D_{\mathrm{Sch}}\) such that \[d_{\mathrm{Sch}}(f;g)\le D_{\mathrm{Sch}}\!\left(n,m,\deg f,\max_i\deg g_i,\frac{\|f\|}{f_*},\mathcal G(K,g)\right),\] after fixing a coefficient norm \(\|\cdot\|\), a normalization of \(K\), and geometric data \(\mathcal G(K,g)\). The computational resource bounded is the maximum degree \(2d\) in the preordering certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity on a compact basic set has a finite preordering certificate; effective results bound its degree using dimensions, degrees, normalized margin, and geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Effective Schmüdgen Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative Schmüdgen finiteness statement is standard, but this exact leaf requires an effective complexity bound. No source identifies a computable bound, its normalization, or the geometric parameters on which it depends, so the schematic function cannot yet be reviewed as a mathematical bound.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a finite order \(d\) such that \(f\in M_d(g)\); an effective Putinar bound controls the least such \(d\).

notation.meaning: Least truncated-quadratic-module order certifying the polynomial.
Positive minimum of the polynomial on the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The Archimedean quadratic-module version of Putinar's theorem is intended.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Putinar positivity implies \(d_{\mathrm{Put}}(f;g)<\infty\). An effective version fixes a coefficient norm and an Archimedean witness, then provides a computable function \(D_{\mathrm{Put}}\) satisfying \[d_{\mathrm{Put}}(f;g)\le D_{\mathrm{Put}}\!\left(n,m,\deg f,\max_i\deg g_i,\frac{\|f\|}{f_*},\mathcal A(g)\right),\] where \(\mathcal A(g)\) records quantitative data of the Archimedean witness. The bounded resource is the maximum degree \(2d\) of the SOS-weighted-generator certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an Archimedean condition, strict positivity has a finite quadratic-module certificate; effective bounds depend on degrees, normalized margin, and quantitative Archimedean data.
knowledge_statements.title: Effective Putinar Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative Putinar conclusion under an Archimedean hypothesis is standard, but the proposed effective bound uses an undefined quantitative witness tuple and has no supporting source. A specific effective Putinar theorem and its normalization are required.

assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m,f\in\mathbb Z[x]\) have degree at most \(\delta\) and coefficient bit-size at most \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a finite preordering certificate \(-1=\sum_{I\subseteq[m]}\sigma_Ig_I\); effective Krivine–Stengle results bound its degree and coefficient size in terms of \(n,m,\delta,\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The infeasibility form is used to make the effective resource and input model explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Krivine–Stengle infeasibility yields sums of squares \(\sigma_I\in\Sigma[x]\) satisfying \[-1=\sum_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}}\sigma_Ig_I.\] In the integer-coefficient Turing model, an effective bound is a computable pair \((D,B)\) depending only on \((n,m,\delta,\tau)\) such that the certificate can be chosen with \(\deg(\sigma_Ig_I)\le D\) and coefficient bit-size at most \(B\). Exact rates require a specified effective Positivstellensatz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an empty integer-defined basic semialgebraic set, effective Krivine–Stengle theory bounds the degree and coefficient size of a preordering refutation of minus one.
knowledge_statements.title: Effective Krivine–Stengle Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The infeasibility form is appropriate for a Krivine-Stengle complexity-bound leaf, but the assumptions introduce f without using it, and no effective Positivstellensatz is cited for the claimed degree and coefficient-size dependence. The encoding and coefficient-size convention also require a precise source.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in H_D(\ell)\) is an LP feasibility condition with at most \(\binom{m+D}{D}\) nonnegative coefficient variables.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-level representation size without asserting an unsupported sufficient degree for every positive polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For affine generators \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m\), define \[H_D(\ell)=\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^m,\ |\alpha|\le D}c_\alpha\ell^\alpha:c_\alpha\ge0\right\}.\] This representation has at most \(\binom{m+D}{D}\) nonnegative coefficient variables. Testing \(f\in H_D(\ell)\) is linear-programming feasibility obtained by equating polynomial coefficients; coincident or linearly dependent products can reduce the actual formulation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At product degree D, Handelman membership is an LP with at most binomial(m+D,D) nonnegative product coefficients.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Level Handelman LP Size

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is a compact polytope with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some finite \(D\), \(f=\sum_{|\alpha|\le D}c_\alpha\prod_i\ell_i^{\alpha_i}\) with \(c_\alpha\ge0\); an effective bound controls the least such \(D\).

notation.meaning: Strict positivity margin on the polytope.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral certificates are interpreted as nonnegative combinations of products of affine facet inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(d_H(f;\ell)\) as the least \(D\) for which \[f=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^m,\ |\alpha|\le D}c_\alpha\prod_{i=1}^m\ell_i^{\alpha_i},\qquad c_\alpha\ge0.\] Handelman's theorem gives \(d_H(f;\ell)<\infty\). After normalizing the facet functions, an effective polyhedral bound has the form \(d_H(f;\ell)\le D_H(n,m,\deg f,\|f\|/f_*,\mathcal G(P,\ell))\). The resource is maximum product degree, equivalently the linear-programming certificate level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial strictly positive on a full-dimensional compact polytope has a finite Handelman certificate whose product degree can be bounded using margin and polytope geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Effective Polyhedral-Certificate Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative Handelman representation fits the polyhedral-certificate leaf, but the effective claim is only schematic. A cited theorem must define the facet normalization, polynomial norm, geometric parameters, and explicit or computable dependence of the product degree.

assumptions_latex: A positively homogeneous polynomial norm \(\|\cdot\|\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(f;K):=\|f\|/f_*\) is invariant under replacing \(f\) by \(cf\) for \(c>0\).

notation.meaning: Strict positivity margin of f on K.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a scale-consistent margin parameter without asserting universal dependence or a universal rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polynomial strictly positive on compact \(K\), let \(f_*:=\min_K f>0\). Relative to a fixed positively homogeneous norm, the normalized inverse margin is \[\kappa(f;K):=\frac{\|f\|}{f_*}.\] For every \(c>0\), \(\kappa(cf;K)=\kappa(f;K)\). A degree bound is positivity-margin-sensitive when its stated estimate depends on this or another specified separation-from-zero parameter; whether it does so and with what rate is theorem-specific.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized inverse margin is coefficient size divided by the positive minimum; it is invariant under positive scaling, while its role in a degree bound is theorem-specific.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Positivity Margin

assumptions_latex: The cones \(C_d\) are closed subsets of a fixed finite-dimensional polynomial space and satisfy \(C_d\subseteq C_{d+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{d:f+\varepsilon\in C_d\}\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: Closed degree-indexed certificate cone in the fixed ambient space.
Least certificate order for the positive perturbation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conditional but exact obstruction to uniform bounded order as the positivity margin vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_0\subseteq C_1\subseteq\cdots\) be closed certificate cones in a fixed finite-dimensional polynomial space. Suppose \(f\notin C_d\) for every \(d\), while \(f+\varepsilon\in\bigcup_dC_d\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). If \[d(\varepsilon):=\min\{d:f+\varepsilon\in C_d\},\] then \(d(\varepsilon)\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Thus a uniformly bounded order near this zero-margin boundary would contradict closedness of a fixed truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed nested certificate cones, positive perturbations of an uncertified boundary polynomial require unbounded order as their margin tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order Divergence Near an Uncertified Boundary
knowledge_statements.title: Order Divergence Near an Uncertified Boundary

assumptions_latex: A coefficient norm \(\|\cdot\|\) and normalization of \(K\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Effective certificate orders are governed by the scale-invariant inverse margin \(\kappa(f;K)=\|f\|/f_*\), and typically deteriorate as \(f_*\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This isolates the scale-invariant margin parameter common to effective positivity theorems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every scalar \(c>0\), \(\kappa(cf;K)=\|cf\|/\min_K(cf)=\kappa(f;K)\). Thus a scale-consistent degree estimate may depend on \(f\) through \(\kappa(f;K)\), rather than through \(f_*\) alone. In effective SOS, preordering, or polyhedral certificates, a bound is commonly expressible as \(d\le D(\kappa(f;K),\mathcal P)\), where \(\mathcal P\) collects degrees and geometric data; no uniform bounded order is implied as \(f_*\to0\) with \(\|f\|\) fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relevant positivity parameter is usually coefficient size divided by the positive minimum; it is scale invariant, and degree bounds worsen near the positivity boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Positivity-Margin Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scale invariance of the ratio ||f||/f_* is mathematically correct, but the broader assertion that effective certificate orders are governed by this ratio and deteriorate as the margin vanishes is theorem-dependent. A source for a specific certificate family and quantitative bound is required.

assumptions_latex: A certificate family and a normalization of coordinates and defining data are fixed.
The bound concerns a specified truncation-order convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A degree estimate is geometry-sensitive when its stated upper bound depends on normalized quantitative geometric data beyond dimensions and polynomial degrees.

notation.meaning: The theorem-specific tuple of normalized geometric data.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of quantitative bounds; it does not claim that every effective theorem requires a separate universal geometry tuple.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a certificate family and normalization have been fixed, a degree estimate is geometry-sensitive if its stated upper bound depends on quantitative geometric data \(\mathcal G\), such as a normalized containing radius, interior thickness, facet conditioning, or quantitative Archimedean-witness data. The admissible tuple \(\mathcal G\) is theorem-specific; these examples are not interchangeable, and geometry sensitivity of an upper-bound formula is not by itself a claim about the intrinsic least certificate order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound is geometry-sensitive when, under fixed normalization, its formula depends on theorem-specific geometric conditioning data.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Sensitive Degree Bounds

assumptions_latex: The target and every generator are transformed together.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in M_d(g)\iff f\circ\phi\in M_d(g\circ\phi)\), with the analogous equivalence for truncated preorderings.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates intrinsic exact order from coordinate-dependent numerical estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(y)=Ay+b\) with \(A\) invertible, and set \(\widetilde f=f\circ\phi\) and \(\widetilde g_i=g_i\circ\phi\). Composition with \(\phi\) preserves total degree and sums of squares and is inverted by composition with \(\phi^{-1}\). Therefore \[f\in M_d(g)\iff\widetilde f\in M_d(\widetilde g),\] with the analogous equivalence for truncated preorderings. Exact least order is invariant, although coordinate norms, radii, and conditioning parameters in a chosen estimate may change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible affine coordinate changes preserve exact total-degree certificate order even though coordinate-based estimates may change.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Invariance of Exact Certificate Order
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Invariance of Exact Certificate Order

assumptions_latex: A normalization of the ambient coordinates and generators is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A quantitative certificate-degree bound must include geometric conditioning data; dimension and polynomial degrees alone do not encode proximity to degeneracy.

notation.meaning: A chosen geometric conditioning tuple for the presentation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry may include radius, diameter, interior thickness, constraint scaling, or Archimedean-witness data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After fixing a certificate family, an effective estimate has the schematic form \[d\le D\!\left(n,m,\deg f,\max_i\deg g_i,\frac{\|f\|}{\min_K f},\mathcal G(K,g)\right).\] The tuple \(\mathcal G(K,g)\) records quantitative geometry relevant to the selected theorem, such as a containing radius, an interior-thickness parameter, facet conditioning, or the size and degree of an Archimedean witness. Rescaling coordinates or generators changes these quantities and can change the numerical degree estimate without changing the abstract feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Effective degree estimates depend on quantitative conditioning of the set and its presentation, such as radius, thickness, facet scaling, or an Archimedean witness.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Sensitive Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle is plausible and locally relevant, but the assertion that every quantitative degree bound must include separate geometric conditioning data is stronger than the displayed schematic examples establish. A specific theorem or lower-bound result must identify the applicable geometry parameters and justify the necessity claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Generator-Sensitive Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines sensitivity to a particular polynomial presentation of a basic closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K(g)=\{x:g_i(x)\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), a degree bound for membership \(f\in M_N(g)\) is generator-sensitive if the bound depends on presentation data of \(g\), such as \(m\), \(d_g\), generator coefficient heights, or conditioning constants, rather than only on the set \(K(g)\). Consequently, two tuples \(g\) and \(h\) with \(K(g)=K(h)\) may receive different guaranteed truncation orders when their relevant presentation data differ. Generator sensitivity is therefore a property of the stated bound relative to the chosen description, not an invariant of \(K(g)\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate degree bound is generator-sensitive when its guaranteed truncation order depends on the chosen defining polynomials and can differ between descriptions of the same feasible set.
assumptions_latex: For \(N\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(M_N(g)\) contain representations \(\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i\) with every summand of degree at most \(2N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A truncation bound is generator-sensitive when it depends on quantitative data of the displayed generators, not merely on their feasible set.

Degree-\(2N\) truncation of the quadratic module.

These counts concern total-degree monomials and do not incorporate sparsity or symmetry reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Gram-Matrix Dimension Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures dense Gram-matrix size before exploiting coefficient constraints, sparsity, or symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An SOS representation of \(p\) may be written as
\[
p(x)=v_r(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv_r(x),\qquad Q\succeq0,
\]
where \(v_r\) contains all monomials of total degree at most \(r\). Its length is \(s=\binom{n+r}{r}\). Hence the associated positive-semidefinite block has matrix order \(s\) and \(s(s+1)/2\) independent scalar entries before coefficient-matching equations are imposed. Dense matrix storage is \(\Theta(s^2)\), and conventional dense Cholesky or eigendecomposition algorithms use \(O(s^3)\) arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For SOS degree 2r in n variables, the dense Gram matrix has binomial(n+r,r) rows, quadratically many independent entries, and conventional dense factorizations have cubic arithmetic cost in its order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dense SOS Gram matrix has order \(\binom{n+r}{r}\) and \(\binom{n+r}{r}(\binom{n+r}{r}+1)/2\) independent symmetric entries.

\[
\dim\ker\mathcal A=\frac{s(s+1)}2-\binom{n+2r}{2r}.
\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses naive rational height as the certificate coefficient-magnitude measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the magnitude, or naive height, of a reduced rational coefficient by
\[
H(c)=\max\{|a|,b\},
\]
with \(H(0)=1\). For a finite rational certificate \(\mathcal C\), define \(H(\mathcal C)=\max_{c\in\operatorname{coeff}(\mathcal C)}H(c)\). A family \((\mathcal C_k)\) exhibits coefficient magnitude growth when \(H(\mathcal C_k)\) is unbounded; a quantitative bound is any function \(B(k)\) satisfying \(H(\mathcal C_k)\le B(k)\). This convention measures numerators and denominators and is distinct from polynomial degree or support size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient magnitude is the largest reduced numerator or denominator appearing in a rational certificate; growth means this height becomes unbounded across a family.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Magnitude Growth

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Bit Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixes a conventional signed binary encoding for reduced rational coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Using signed binary for the numerator and ordinary binary for the positive denominator, define
\[
\ell(c)=1+\left\lceil\log_2(|a|+1)\right\rceil+\left\lceil\log_2(b+1)\right\rceil.
\]
For \(H(c)\ge2\), this gives \(\ell(c)=\Theta(\log H(c))\). For a finite coefficient list \((c_1,\ldots,c_s)\), the coefficient payload has length \(\sum_{j=1}^s\ell(c_j)\), excluding monomial-index and structural metadata. The precise additive overhead depends on the selected self-delimiting or container encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated binary convention, a reduced rational coefficient needs logarithmically many bits in its largest numerator or denominator, and a certificate's coefficient payload sums these costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The binary length of \(c\) is logarithmic in its rational height.

notation.meaning: Binary encoding length of a reduced rational coefficient.

Storing only upper-triangular entries requires \[M=\sum_{i=1}^t\frac{N_i(N_i+1)}2\] rational slots. If every stored entry has binary length at most \(B\), the coefficient payload is \(O(MB)\) bits, plus basis, block, and polynomial-identity metadata. Storing full matrices changes only the constant factor and not the quadratic dependence on each \(N_i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts a direct sparse binary encoding, excluding compression and implementation-specific framing.

Store each rational coefficient in reduced binary form and each exponent vector \(\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^n\), with \(|\alpha|\le d\), by its \(n\) coordinates. The resulting sparse encoding uses
\[
O\!\left(L+sn\log_2(d+1)+s\log_2(t+1)\right)
\]
bits, where \(t\) is the number of certificate blocks or multipliers and the final term records block indices. For a dense fixed-order basis, exponent indices may instead be implicit, leaving coefficient payload \(L\) plus block metadata. The bound concerns storage, not arithmetic running time.

children.title: Precision Requirements for Recovery
children.top_down_role: Numerical precision demands associated with recovering exact coefficient data.

assumptions_latex: No a priori denominator, height, or other separation bound is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists\varepsilon>0\) that guarantees unique recovery of every \(c\in\mathbb Q\) from every \(\widetilde c\) satisfying \(|\widetilde c-c|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic boundary for exact rational recovery from finite-precision approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist distinct rationals \(r,s\in\mathbb Q\) with \(|r-s|<2\varepsilon\). Consequently, some \(\widetilde c\in\mathbb R\) satisfies both \(|\widetilde c-r|<\varepsilon\) and \(|\widetilde c-s|<\varepsilon\). Therefore no fixed positive absolute-error tolerance uniquely recovers an arbitrary rational coefficient unless a denominator or height bound, or another separation condition, is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rationals have no positive uniform separation, so finite precision cannot guarantee exact rational recovery without a denominator, height, or equivalent separation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Uniform Recovery Without a Height Bound
knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Recovery Without a Height Bound

assumptions_latex: Let \(c=a/b\) be reduced with \(1\le b\le Q\), and let \(\widetilde c\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Error below \(1/(2Q^2)\) uniquely determines \(c\) among rationals with denominator at most \(Q\).

notation.meaning: Known upper bound on the reduced denominator.
Numerical approximation to the exact coefficient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States a sufficient coordinatewise precision threshold for bounded-denominator rational recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If
\[
|\widetilde c-c|<\frac{1}{2Q^2},
\]
then \(c\) is the unique rational number with reduced denominator at most \(Q\) lying within that radius of \(\widetilde c\), and continued-fraction reconstruction recovers it. Thus a certificate whose coefficients all have denominators at most \(Q\) is recoverable coordinatewise under the same absolute-error bound. After reconstruction, exact polynomial identities and positive-semidefiniteness conditions must still be checked; proximity alone does not certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Knowing a denominator bound Q, absolute coefficient error below 1/(2Q^2) permits unique rational reconstruction, followed by exact certificate verification.
knowledge_statements.title: Precision Requirements for Recovery

children.title: Degree-Bound Nonstability Barrier
children.top_down_role: Structural nonexistence phenomena limiting uniform quantitative representations.

assumptions_latex: Let \(M\subseteq\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be a quadratic module with degree truncations \(M_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform degree bounds fail exactly when some bounded-degree finite-dimensional family requires arbitrarily large certificate truncation.

notation.meaning: Degree-truncated part of the certificate cone.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulates the nonexistence of bounds controlled solely by bounded polynomial input spaces.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Quadratic Modules and Preorderings p. 60

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There is no uniform degree bound on \(M\) over finite-dimensional input spaces if there exists a finite-dimensional subspace \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}[x]\) such that, for every \(N\in\mathbb{N}\),
\[
(M\cap U)\nsubseteq M_N.
\]
Equivalently, one can choose \(f_N\in M\cap U\) whose every quadratic-module representation has a summand of degree greater than \(2N\). Since \(U\) has bounded polynomial degree, certificate degree cannot then be bounded by input degree alone, even though each individual \(f_N\) belongs to \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform degree bounds fail when bounded-degree polynomials in the module can require certificate representations of arbitrarily high degree.
knowledge_statements.title: Absence of Uniform Degree Bounds

with all \(q_{ij}\in W\). Equivalently, no degree bound depending only on \(U\) controls the square factors in representations of all members of \(M(g)\cap U\).

Therefore replacing V by a proper subspace can remove valid certificates; for example, (x+1)^2 is representable over \operatorname{span}\{1,x\} but not over \operatorname{span}\{x\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coordinate invariant of equal-span polynomial basis selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) and \(w\) be ordered bases of the same finite-dimensional polynomial space \(V\). For a fixed polynomial \(p\), define \(r_v(p)=\min\{\operatorname{rank}Q:Q\succeq0,\ p=v^{\mathsf T}Qv\}\), with value \(+\infty\) when the set is empty, and define \(r_w(p)\) analogously. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Change-of-basis rule for SOS Gram representations of a fixed polynomial space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subset\mathbb R[x]\) be finite-dimensional, let \(v(x)\) and \(w(x)\) be ordered bases of \(V\), and suppose \(w(x)=T v(x)\) for an invertible matrix \(T\). Then \(p(x)=v(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv(x)\) if and only if \(p(x)=w(x)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Qw(x)\), where \(\widetilde Q=T^{-\mathsf T}QT^{-1}\). Moreover, \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(\widetilde Q\succeq0\). Thus basis selection changes Gram-matrix coordinates but neither the represented polynomial nor existence of a positive-semidefinite Gram certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible polynomial-basis change transforms the Gram matrix by congruence, preserving both the polynomial and positive semidefiniteness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular Monomial Scaling Can Lose the Gram Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of diagonal scaling when a scaling factor vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_m)\) has some \(d_i=0\), then \(Dz\) no longer spans the same polynomial space as \(z\), no inverse-congruence Gram transformation exists, and SOS feasibility need not be preserved. For example, with \(z=(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\), the polynomial \((1+x)^2\) has a PSD Gram representation in \(z\) but none in \(Dz=(0,x)^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero scaling factor is not a harmless rescaling: it can remove a basis direction and destroy an existing Gram certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ singular}\not\Longrightarrow\text{preservation of the Gram-representable SOS cone}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral effect of nonsingular diagonal monomial scaling on a positive-definite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), let \(D\) be nonsingular diagonal, and put \(\widehat Q=D^{-\mathsf T}QD^{-1}\). Then \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)/\|D\|_2^2\le\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q)\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(\widehat Q)\le\lambda_{\max}(Q)\|D^{-1}\|_2^2\). Consequently, \(\kappa_2(\widehat Q)\le\kappa_2(Q)\kappa_2(D)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal monomial scaling can change Gram conditioning by up to the square of the scaling matrix's condition number.

Then \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\) if and only if \(p=\widehat z^{\mathsf T}\widehat Q\widehat z\), where \(\widehat Q=D^{-\mathsf T}QD^{-1}\). Moreover, \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(\widehat Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular diagonal monomial scaling transforms Gram matrices by inverse congruence and preserves PSD certificate feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z^{\mathsf T}Qz=(Dz)^{\mathsf T}(D^{-\mathsf T}QD^{-1})(Dz),\qquad Q\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow D^{-\mathsf T}QD^{-1}\succeq0.

For every symmetric matrix \(Q\), the identity \(p(x)=z(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz(x)\) is equivalent to \(p(x)=\widehat z(x)^{\mathsf T}\widehat Q\widehat z(x)\), with \(\widehat Q=D^{-\mathsf T}QD^{-1}\). Because this is an invertible congruence, \(Q\succeq0\) exactly when \(\widehat Q\succeq0\). Scaling may alter numerical conditioning but not certificate feasibility.

children.title: Orthogonal Basis Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Conditioning behavior associated with orthogonal polynomial bases.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of the quadratic Gram synthesis map in an orthonormal polynomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let w_1,\ldots,w_m be orthonormal in L^2(\mu), assume w_iw_j\in L^2(\mu), and define \mathcal G(Q)=w^{\mathsf T}Qw. Choose symmetric coordinate matrices F^{ij} satisfying w^{\mathsf T}F^{ij}w=w_iw_j. Then \langle\mathcal G(F^{ij}),\mathcal G(F^{k\ell})\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}=\int w_iw_jw_kw_\ell\,d\mu. Thus orthonormality of the w_i does not imply that \mathcal G has condition number one on the complement of its kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonality of basis polynomials does not orthogonalize their products; Gram-map conditioning depends on fourth-order product moments.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G is restricted to the orthogonal complement of its kernel when a finite condition number is discussed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \langle\mathcal G(F^{ij}),\mathcal G(F^{k\ell})\rangle=\int w_iw_jw_kw_\ell\,d\mu,\quad\text{and generally }\kappa(\mathcal G)\ne1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Construction from a Positive-Definite Moment Gramian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional construction of an orthonormal polynomial basis for a chosen measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_m)^{\mathsf T}\) have entries in \(L^2(\mu)\), and form \(H=\int vv^{\mathsf T}\,d\mu\). If \(H\succ0\) and \(H=LL^{\mathsf T}\), then \(w=L^{-1}v\) satisfies \(\int ww^{\mathsf T}\,d\mu=I\). If \(H\) is singular, the listed functions are dependent in \(L^2(\mu)\), so an invertible orthonormalization of the full list is impossible until dependent directions are removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cholesky whitening of a positive-definite moment Gramian constructs an orthonormal polynomial basis; singularity identifies directions that must be removed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w=L^{-1}v\Longrightarrow\int ww^{\mathsf T}d\mu=I.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orthonormal Factors with a Singular Product Gramian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of product independence despite perfect orthonormality of the factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu=\tfrac12(\delta_{-1}+\delta_1)\), \(w_1(x)=1\), and \(w_2(x)=x\). Then \(w_1,w_2\) are orthonormal in \(L^2(\mu)\), but \(w_1^2=w_2^2\) in \(L^2(\mu)\). Consequently, for \(\mathcal G(Q)=w^{\mathsf T}Qw\), the nonzero matrix \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\) belongs to \(\ker\mathcal G\), and the Gramian of the product family \(\{w_iw_j\}\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the two-point measure, 1 and x are orthonormal although their squares coincide, so quadratic Gram synthesis has a nontrivial kernel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle w_i,w_j\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}=\delta_{ij}\), while \(\mathcal G(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1))=1-x^2=0\) in \(L^2(\mu)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear coefficient-synthesis conditioning in an orthonormal polynomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subset L^2(\mu)\) be finite-dimensional and let \(w_1,\ldots,w_m\) be an orthonormal basis. For \(S:\mathbb R^m\to V\), \(Sc=\sum_i c_iw_i\), one has \(\|Sc\|_{L^2(\mu)}=\|c\|_2\). Hence \(S\) has condition number one between these norms. This does not imply that the quadratic Gram map \(Q\mapsto w^{\mathsf T}Qw\) is an isometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient synthesis in an orthonormal basis is perfectly conditioned, although quadratic Gram synthesis can remain ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left\|\sum_i c_iw_i\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}=\|c\|_2,\qquad \kappa_2(S)=1.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthonormal Synthesis Is an Isometry
Orthogonal Basis Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of coefficient matching under an orthonormal polynomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subset L^2(\mu)\) be finite-dimensional and let \(w_1,\ldots,w_m\) be an orthonormal basis of \(V\), so \(\langle w_i,w_j\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}=\delta_{ij}\). The synthesis map \(S:\mathbb R^m\to V\), defined by \(Sc=\sum_{i=1}^m c_iw_i\), is an isometry: \(\|Sc\|_{L^2(\mu)}=\|c\|_2\). Hence its Euclidean-to-\(L^2(\mu)\) condition number is \(1\). This statement concerns basis synthesis; it does not guarantee that the full SOS coefficient-matching operator is well-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthonormal polynomial basis makes coefficient synthesis an isometry, although the complete Gram coefficient-matching system may remain ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left\|\sum_{i=1}^m c_iw_i\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}=\|c\|_2\) and \(\kappa_2(S)=1\).

notation.meaning: Measure defining the polynomial inner product.

The coefficient of \(x^\alpha\) in \(p\) is \(\sum_{i,j=1}^m c_{ij,\alpha}Q_{ij}\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix z(x)\in\mathbb R[x]^m and 0\le r\le m. There exists Q\succeq0 with \operatorname{rank}(Q)\le r and p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz if and only if there exists Y\in\mathbb R^{m\times r} such that p=z^{\mathsf T}YY^{\mathsf T}z=\|Y^{\mathsf T}z\|_2^2. Coefficient matching in Y is quadratic and generally nonconvex; infeasibility at rank cap r does not exclude higher-rank Gram certificates.

Low-Rank Gram Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between Gram rank and the number of squared polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a polynomial vector \(z(x)\in\mathbb R[x]^m\). If \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^m\) has rank \(r\) and \(p(x)=z(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz(x)\), then any factorization \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\) with \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\) yields \(p(x)=\sum_{k=1}^r q_k(x)^2\), where \(q(x)=Rz(x)\). Conversely, every representation \(p=\sum_{k=1}^r q_k^2\) with each \(q_k\) in the span of the entries of \(z\) produces a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix of rank at most \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r positive-semidefinite Gram matrix gives r polynomial squares, and r supported squares give a Gram matrix of rank at most r.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\Longrightarrow p=\sum_{k=1}^r q_k^2\), with the converse yielding \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)\le r\).

e k\). SAGE search decomposes \(c\) into AGE coefficient vectors and imposes these constraints with exact coefficient matching. For polynomials on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), use \(x_i=e^{y_i}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAGE search decomposes a signomial into one-negative-term AGE blocks certified by balance and relative-entropy constraints.
assumptions_latex: Each AGE block has at most one coefficient not constrained to be nonnegative.
Relative entropy uses its lower-semicontinuous boundary convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{feasible AGE decomposition}\Longrightarrow s(y)\ge0\quad\forall y\in\mathbb R^n.

notation.meaning: relative entropy with the standard boundary convention

knowledge_statements.title: SAGE Relative-Entropy Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Template-relative separation for fixed-support SAGE membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the closed fixed-support SAGE coefficient cone \(C_{\mathrm{SAGE}}(A)\), \(c\notin C_{\mathrm{SAGE}}(A)\) if and only if some coefficient functional \(w\) satisfies \(\langle w,q\rangle\ge0\) for every \(q\in C_{\mathrm{SAGE}}(A)\) and \(\langle w,c\rangle<0\). This proves only failure of the selected SAGE cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator can certify failure of fixed-support SAGE membership, but not polynomial negativity.
assumptions_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{SAGE}}(A)\) is taken with its closed-cone convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c\notin C_{\mathrm{SAGE}}(A)\iff\exists w\in C_{\mathrm{SAGE}}(A)^*:\langle w,c\rangle<0.
knowledge_statements.title: SAGE Dual Separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain extension for polynomial certificates obtained through logarithmic substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a polynomial \(p\) is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), continuity extends the conclusion to \(\mathbb R_+^n\). It does not extend it to \(\mathbb R^n\): for example, \(p(x)=x\) is positive on \(\mathbb R_{++}\) but negative for \(x<0\). All-space validity requires parity or sign-symmetry conditions, or separate orthant certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-orthant polynomial validity extends to its closure, but not automatically to other orthants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\ge0\text{ on }\mathbb R_{++}^n\Longrightarrow p\ge0\text{ on }\mathbb R_+^n,\quad\text{not generally on }\mathbb R^n.
knowledge_statements.title: Orthant-Closure and All-Space Boundary
Relative-Entropy Polynomial Certificate Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic search for signomial-based polynomial nonnegativity certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(p(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha x^\alpha\) and a prescribed decomposition into signomial nonnegativity blocks after restricting to \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) and substituting \(x_i=\exp(y_i)\). Introduce block coefficients and auxiliary relative-entropy variables, impose exact coefficient matching to \(c\), and impose the relative-entropy-cone constraints required by every block. Solve the resulting convex feasibility problem and output the block decomposition when feasible. Its validity certifies \(p(x)\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\); boundary or all-space claims require separate closure and sign-symmetry conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a logarithmic substitution, coefficient matching and relative-entropy cones search for structured nonnegativity decompositions on the positive orthant.
assumptions_latex: A fixed relative-entropy-representable block template is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{feasible block data}\Longrightarrow p(x)\ge0\text{ for every }x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
review_flags: The intended relative-entropy certificate family is not identified uniquely.
A source is required for its exact cone constraints and domain extension.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-orthant restriction and warning about boundary and all-space extensions are appropriate, but the relative-entropy certificate family and its block constraints are not specified. A source is needed to determine the exact algorithm and sufficient hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness radius for scalar bounded-denominator rational reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B\in\mathbb N. Distinct reduced rationals with positive denominators at most B are separated by at least B^{-2}. Hence an open interval of radius (2B^2)^{-1} contains at most one such rational.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently small neighborhood contains at most one reduced rational whose denominator is bounded by B.
assumptions_latex: Candidate rationals are reduced and have positive denominator at most B.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\widehat x-a/b|<(2B^2)^{-1}\Longrightarrow a/b\text{ is the unique denominator-}\le B\text{ rational in that neighborhood}.
review_flags: Uniqueness does not establish that the reconstructed value is part of a valid Gram certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Denominator Reconstruction Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous reconstruction inside the exact coefficient-matching affine space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the rational coefficient equations be \(Aq=b\). Compute exactly a particular solution \(q_0\in\mathbb Q^s\) and a rational nullspace matrix \(N\) such that every solution is \(q=q_0+Nt\). Estimate \(\widehat t\) from a numerical Gram vector, reconstruct a rational \(t\) under prescribed denominator bounds, and set \(q=q_0+Nt\). Then \(Aq=b\) holds identically. Accept the associated symmetric matrix \(Q\) only after exact positive-semidefiniteness verification; otherwise increase precision or bounds, change parameterization, or report failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterizing the exact affine Gram slice first permits simultaneous rational reconstruction without violating shared coefficient equations.
assumptions_latex: \(q_0\) and \(N\) are computed exactly over \(\mathbb Q\).
The reconstructed parameter vector is rational.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q=q_0+Nt\Longrightarrow Aq=b;\qquad Q\succeq0\Longrightarrow p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\text{ is an exact rational Gram certificate}.
review_flags: Reconstructing affine parameters avoids inconsistent entrywise reconstruction.
Exact affine membership does not imply positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Parameter Rational Gram Reconstruction
Rational Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of an exact rational Gram certificate from numerical SDP output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(p\in\mathbb Q[x]\), a basis vector \(z\in\mathbb Q[x]^m\), a numerical symmetric matrix \(\widehat Q\), and a denominator bound \(B\). Reconstruct rational entries near \(\widehat Q\), then project them exactly onto the affine coefficient-matching space \(\mathcal A=\{Q\in\mathbb S^m:p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\}\). Accept and output \(Q\in\mathcal A\cap\mathbb S_+^m\) only after exact coefficient comparison and an exact positive-semidefiniteness test. Otherwise increase precision or \(B\), or report reconstruction failure; numerical proximity alone is not a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover a rational Gram matrix near a numerical solution, then accept it only after exact identity and positive-semidefiniteness checks.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat Q=\widehat Q^{\mathsf T}\) is numerical Gram data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\), \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\), and \(Q\succeq0\) constitute an exact rational certificate.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports the reconstruction and exact PSD-validation procedure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is appropriately scoped and correctly refuses to treat numerical proximity as certification. No source locator supports the rational reconstruction, affine correction, and exact PSD-validation procedure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correction Within a Certified PSD Margin
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient spectral condition ensuring that an exact symbolic correction preserves PSD.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \widehat Q\in\mathbb S^m be represented exactly, let E\in\mathbb S^m be an exact symbolic correction, and set Q=\widehat Q+E. If rigorous bounds satisfy \underline\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q), \eta\ge\|E\|_2, and \underline\lambda-\eta\ge0, then Q\succeq0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact correction preserves positive semidefiniteness when its norm does not exceed a certified lower spectral margin.
assumptions_latex: E\in\mathbb S^m is an exact correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \underline\lambda-\eta\ge0\Longrightarrow Q=\widehat Q+E\succeq0.

notation.meaning: Rigorous upper bound on the correction norm.

review_flags: A negative or unresolved margin is inconclusive and does not disprove PSD.
knowledge_statements.title: Correction Within a Certified PSD Margin

assumptions_latex: The residual equation has a symmetric exact solution \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(E)=b-\mathcal A(\widehat Q)\Longrightarrow\mathcal A(\widehat Q+E)=b\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector of the target polynomial.

review_flags: Exact identity correction alone does not establish positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correction of represented numerical Gram data onto the polynomial coefficient-matching affine space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^m\to\mathbb Q^N\) be the rational linear coefficient map \(\mathcal A(Q)=\operatorname{coeff}(z^{\mathsf T}Qz)\), and let \(b=\operatorname{coeff}(p)\). Given an exactly represented candidate \(\widehat Q\), solve \(\mathcal A(E)=b-\mathcal A(\widehat Q)\) in exact arithmetic. Every symmetric solution gives \(Q=\widehat Q+E\) with \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\) exactly; certification still requires an exact proof that \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the exact coefficient-residual system to restore the Gram identity; positive semidefiniteness remains a separate exact check.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Affine Identity Correction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational workflow joining numerical discovery to independently checkable exact acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a numerical Gram candidate \(\widehat Q\), recover exactly represented data and solve the exact residual equations needed to obtain a symmetric \(Q\) with \(\mathcal A(Q)=\operatorname{coeff}(p)\). Verify coefficientwise that \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\), and establish \(Q\succeq0\) by an exact factorization, a complete exact principal-minor test, an exact PSD-preserving elimination, or a rigorous spectral enclosure proving a nonnegative lower eigenvalue bound. Accept only if every required check succeeds; a failed or unresolved recovery, identity, or PSD check yields no certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discover numerically, recover and correct exactly, and accept only after rigorous identity and PSD verification; unresolved checks yield no certificate.
assumptions_latex: The numerical candidate can be represented or recovered exactly.
Final identity and PSD decisions use exact or rigorously validated arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{accept}(Q)\Longrightarrow p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\text{ and }Q\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Exactly recovered and corrected Gram matrix.
Exact coefficient map for the selected Gram basis.

review_flags: Soundness does not imply successful recovery for every numerical candidate.
A tolerance-based or unresolved PSD decision cannot justify acceptance.
knowledge_statements.title: End-to-End Symbolic-Numeric Certification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete exact positive-semidefiniteness test for a recovered symbolic Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\) be symmetric. Then \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(\det Q[I,I]\ge0\) for every \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric rational matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when all its principal minors are nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: All determinants and comparisons are evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow \det Q[I,I]\ge0\quad\text{for every }I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}.
review_flags: Checking only leading principal minors is insufficient for positive semidefiniteness.
The complete test has exponentially many principal minors.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Principal-Minor PSD Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exactly checkable positive-semidefiniteness witness for a recovered Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\) be symmetric. If exact matrices \(L\in\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\) and diagonal \(\Delta\in\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\) satisfy \(L\) invertible, \(Q=L\Delta L^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\Delta_{ii}\ge0\) for every \(i\), then \(Q\succeq0\). Hence an exact identity \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\) together with these checks certifies that \(p\) is a sum of squares over \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact invertible congruence to a nonnegative diagonal matrix is a finite PSD witness for a recovered Gram matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is invertible and \(\Delta\) is diagonal with nonnegative entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\succeq0;\qquad p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\Longrightarrow p=(L^{\mathsf T}z)^{\mathsf T}\Delta(L^{\mathsf T}z)\in\Sigma\mathbb R[x]^2.
review_flags: Approximate factorization is not an exact PSD witness.
The resulting square coefficients may lie in an exact real algebraic extension even when the matrix data are rational.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Congruence-Diagonal PSD Witness

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\) is recovered from numerical data.
Exact arithmetic is used for every acceptance check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\), and \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\Longrightarrow p=\sum_k(Rz)_k^2\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers symbolic-numeric SOS certification.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certification obtained by correcting and verifying numerical certificate data symbolically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb Q[x]\), let \(z\in\mathbb Q[x]^m\), and let \(\widehat Q\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be a numerical approximation to a Gram matrix. A symbolic-numeric certificate consists of exact data \(Q\in\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\) obtained from \(\widehat Q\), together with exact verification that \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\), and \(Q\succeq0\). Positive semidefiniteness may be verified by an exact factorization \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\) over an exact ordered field. Once these checks pass, the floating-point computation is only a discovery mechanism and \(p=\sum_k(Rz)_k^2\) is independently checkable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical data become a certificate only after exact symbolic correction, coefficient verification, and an exact positive-semidefiniteness check.
knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic-Numeric Certification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient uniform PSD test for a symmetric interval Gram enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let [Q]=\{Q\in\mathbb S^m:|Q-Q_c|\le R\}, with R\ge0 entrywise. If rigorous bounds satisfy \underline\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(Q_c), \rho\ge\|R\|_2, and \underline\lambda-\rho\ge0, then every Q\in[Q] is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorous midpoint eigenvalue bound exceeding the interval-radius norm certifies every enclosed symmetric matrix as positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \underline\lambda-\rho\ge0\Longrightarrow (\forall Q\in[Q])\ Q\succeq0.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound for the midpoint's smallest eigenvalue.

review_flags: This is sufficient but not necessary; failure of the bound is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.title: Midpoint-Radius PSD Validation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coefficientwise Zero Containment Need Not Give a Common Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of naive coefficientwise interval-zero containment for coupled Gram data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let p(x)=x, z(x)=1+x, and [Q]=[0,1] in the scalar Gram model z^{\mathsf T}Qz=Q(1+2x+x^2). The interval residual coefficients are [-1,0], [-1,1], and [-1,0], each containing zero, but no single Q\in[0,1] satisfies x=Q(1+2x+x^2).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every residual-coefficient interval may contain zero even though no common enclosed Gram value satisfies the polynomial identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in[p-z^{\mathsf T}[Q]z]_\alpha\ \forall\alpha\quad\not\Longrightarrow\quad\exists Q\in[Q]:p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz.

notation.meaning: Interval enclosure of one residual coefficient.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficientwise Zero Containment Need Not Give a Common Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated existence of one common enclosed Gram matrix satisfying all coefficient equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the exact coefficient equations as \(Aq=b\), partition \(A=[B\ C]\) with square nonsingular \(B\), and choose an exactly represented \(q_K\in[q_K]\). If a verified linear solve encloses the exact solution of \(Bq_J=b-Cq_K\) in \([q_J]\subseteq[q_J]^{\mathrm{given}}\), the consistently assembled \([Q']\subseteq[Q]\) contains a matrix \(Q_*\) satisfying every coefficient equation. If a rigorous interval test proves every \(Q\in[Q']\) positive semidefinite, then \(Q_*\succeq0\) and \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Q_*z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified coupled solve establishes one common enclosed matrix satisfying the polynomial identity; uniform PSD validation of its enclosure then certifies it.
assumptions_latex: \(q_K\) is exactly represented and belongs to its prescribed enclosure.
All solves and enclosure tests use outward rounding.
\([Q']\) is assembled consistently from one interval solution vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists Q_*\in[Q']:\mathcal L(Q_*)=p\bigr)\land\bigl(\forall Q\in[Q']:\ Q\succeq0\bigr)\Longrightarrow p=z^{\mathsf T}Q_*z.

notation.meaning: Validated subenclosure containing a common solution matrix.
Gram coefficient map defined by \(z^{\mathsf T}Qz\).

review_flags: This is a sufficient full-row-rank variant; rank-deficient systems require exact elimination or a verified affine solver.
Failure to validate nonsingularity, inclusion, or PSD is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Interval Affine-Feasibility Validation
Interval-Validated Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigorous enclosure test for a polynomial Gram certificate near numerical data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\), let \(z\in\mathbb R[x]^m\), and let \([Q]\) be a symmetric interval matrix produced with outward rounding. An interval-validated certificate must establish both the polynomial identity and positivity: interval evaluation of each coefficient residual in \(p-z^{\mathsf T}Qz\) must be reduced to the singleton \([0,0]\) after validated correction, and a rigorous eigenvalue or factorization bound must prove \(Q\succeq0\) for the selected enclosed matrix. If either enclosure contains unresolved nonzero residuals or permits a negative eigenvalue, certification fails rather than becoming approximate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward-rounded intervals certify a Gram representation only when coefficient residuals vanish rigorously and positive semidefiniteness is conclusively validated.
assumptions_latex: \([Q]\) is symmetric and computed with outward rounding.
Residual and spectral tests use validated interval arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([p-z^{\mathsf T}Qz]=[0,0]\) coefficientwise and a rigorous proof of \(Q\succeq0\) certify \(p(x)\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Outward-rounded interval enclosure of Gram data.
Exact zero interval required for each coefficient residual.

review_flags: The exact validated-correction and interval PSD theorem requires a source.
Naive interval containment of zero is insufficient and is not asserted.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record identifies the two necessary verification obligations, but it does not precisely specify how a single enclosed Gram matrix is selected or how validated correction establishes its exact coefficient identity and PSD property. The missing source is necessary to determine a reliable theorem and algorithmic formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Identity Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact verification of an SOS or quadratic-module polynomial identity by coefficient comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be an exact field, let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in F[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), and let proposed multipliers \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in F[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be given. Define \(r=f-\sigma_0-\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i\), and let \(d\) be any known upper bound on the degrees of the displayed terms. The proposed certificate passes polynomial-identity verification exactly when \([x^\alpha]r=0\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\) with \(|\alpha|\le d\). Equivalently, \(r\) is the zero polynomial in \(F[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\); agreement at finitely many sampled points alone is not an exact identity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand the claimed certificate exactly and compare every coefficient through a valid degree bound. It passes precisely when the residual is the zero polynomial, not merely zero at sampled points.
assumptions_latex: All displayed certificate polynomials have finite explicit representations.
\(d\) bounds the degrees of all terms in the proposed identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i\iff [x^\alpha]r=0\text{ for every }\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\text{ with }|\alpha|\le d.\)

notation.meaning: coefficient of the monomial indexed by alpha in p
residual polynomial of the proposed identity
a finite upper bound on the degrees of the displayed terms

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between semidefinite and strict positive-definite tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rule requiring an ordinary Cholesky factorization with every pivot strictly positive characterizes \(Q\succ0\), not \(Q\succeq0\). Singular matrices such as \(Q=0\) are PSD but fail that rule. Exact PSD verification must permit zero directions, for example through a nonnegative-diagonal exact congruence factorization or nonnegative principal minors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive Cholesky pivots incorrectly reject singular PSD Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\succ0\Longrightarrow Q\succeq0,\qquad Q\succeq0\centernot\Longrightarrow Q\succ0.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-PSD Verification Boundary
Positive-Semidefiniteness Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact PSD verification for Gram matrices occurring in sum-of-squares certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb Q^{N\times N}\) be symmetric. An exact factorization \(P^{\mathsf T}QP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), where \(P\) is a permutation matrix, \(L\) is unit lower triangular over \(\mathbb Q\), and \(D\) is diagonal with nonnegative rational entries, certifies \(Q\succeq0\). Verification consists of exact matrix multiplication, symmetry checking, verification of the declared factor types, and sign checking of every diagonal entry of \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational symmetric matrix is certified positive semidefinite by an exactly verified permuted LDL-transpose factorization whose diagonal entries are nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: The asserted factorization and factor types are checked using exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^{\mathsf T}QP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\ \land\ D_{ii}\ge0\ \forall i\implies Q\succeq0.\)

notation.meaning: Q is positive semidefinite over the real embedding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding-sensitive verification of real-algebraic certificate coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A real algebraic coefficient is exactly order-verifiable when its encoding identifies a unique real root, for example by a square-free polynomial in \(\mathbb Q[t]\) and a rational isolating interval containing exactly that root. Arithmetic and sign tests must use this selected embedding. A defining or minimal polynomial alone is insufficient when distinct real conjugates have different values or signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Real algebraic coefficients require root-identifying embedding data; a polynomial equation alone may not determine their signs.
assumptions_latex: Each algebraic scalar has an exact representation selecting one real root.
The representation supports exact arithmetic and sign determination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{defining data plus root isolation}\Longrightarrow\text{an unambiguous real algebraic value and exact sign}.
knowledge_statements.title: Real-Algebraic Embedding Verification
Coefficient-Field Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification that a certificate belongs to its declared exact coefficient field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an ordered subfield \(F\subseteq\mathbb R\). A polynomial positivity proof object declared over \(F\) passes coefficient-field verification when every coefficient of its polynomials, every entry of its Gram matrices, and every scalar used in its factorizations lies in \(F\); all asserted identities hold in \(F[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\); and every asserted nonnegative scalar is nonnegative under the specified embedding \(F\hookrightarrow\mathbb R\). Thus a floating-point approximation does not constitute an \(F\)-certificate until its entries and all equalities have been reconstructed and checked exactly in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate over a declared field is valid only when all data belong to that field and all identities and sign tests are checked exactly there.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R\) is an explicitly represented ordered field.
Membership and arithmetic in \(F\) are decidable for the supplied data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{field membership, exact identities, and embedded sign checks}\implies\text{a verified }F\text{-certificate}.\)

notation.meaning: specified real embedding used for order tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is internally consistent and the certificate kind matches coefficient-field verification, but no inspectable source supports the stated field-membership, embedding, and exact-reconstruction requirements.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed normalization of certificate equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational residual \(r\) and positive common denominator \(D\), \(r=0\) in \(\mathbb Q[x]\) if and only if \(Dr=0\) in \(\mathbb Z[x]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rational equalities can be cleared to integer equalities.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is divisible by every denominator in \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r=0\iff Dr=0.
review_flags: The equality-preservation claim is correct but its primary home is Polynomial-Identity Verification; it is not a distinct coefficient-field membership or embedding result.
knowledge_statements.title: Rational Denominator Clearing

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns exact coefficient representation, field membership, arithmetic, and order under a selected real embedding. Rational denominator clearing was deferred as primarily an identity-verification normalization. Polynomial equality and matrix PSD logic remain sibling scopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Proof Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact proof-object representation for quadratic-module positivity certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), a proof object for \(f\ge0\) on \(K\) consists of exact Gram matrices \(Q_i\succeq0\), monomial vectors \(v_i\), and the identity \(f=v_0^{\mathsf T}Q_0v_0+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i v_i^{\mathsf T}Q_i v_i\). Its verifier checks the declared coefficient field, dimensions, matrix symmetry and positive semidefiniteness, and the polynomial identity. Once these checks pass, each quadratic form is a sum of squares and evaluation at any \(x\in K\) yields \(f(x)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact positivity proof object packages Gram matrices, monomial bases, and a polynomial identity whose independent checks imply nonnegativity on the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) and all proof-object data use one exact real coefficient field.
Each \(v_i\) is a finite monomial vector of declared dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_i\succeq0\ \forall i\ \land\ f=v_0^{\mathsf T}Q_0v_0+\sum_i g_i v_i^{\mathsf T}Q_i v_i\implies f\ge0\text{ on }K.\)

notation.meaning: exact Gram matrix for the i-th SOS multiplier

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct factor-list alternative to a Gram-matrix proof object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\}\), finite polynomial lists satisfying \(f=\sum_jh_{0j}^2+\sum_i g_i\sum_jh_{ij}^2\) form an exact proof object for \(f\ge0\) on \(K\). Verification requires exact coefficient-field and polynomial-identity checks but no separate Gram-matrix PSD check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Listing the square factors directly gives a proof object whose exact identity proves nonnegativity without a separate PSD test.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_{ij}\) belong to one exactly represented ordered subfield of \(\mathbb R\).
The lists are finite and the identity is checked exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=\sum_jh_{0j}^2+\sum_i g_i\sum_jh_{ij}^2\Longrightarrow f(x)\ge0\quad\forall x\in K.

notation.meaning: basic closed set defined by the inequalities
